info.title: Agrent API
info.description:
Multi-tenant agriculture-operations API. The schema layer in `src/lib/schemas/index.ts` (request bodies) and `src/lib/dto/*.dto.ts` (response shapes) is the single source of truth — this document is generated from those Zod schemas via `npm run openapi:generate`.

`info.version` is intentionally fixed at `0.0.0` and carries no meaning. The API contract version is `x-api-version` at the root of this document, bumped only on a breaking change; `x-minimum-client-version` is the oldest client still served.

sessionCookie.name: next-auth.session-token
sessionCookie.description: NextAuth session cookie. The default for browser clients. `src/middleware.ts` answers an unauthenticated API route with 401 JSON rather than a redirect.

bearerToken.description: Access token from `POST /api/auth/token`, bound to the same UserSession as the cookie. Used by native clients; `auth()` resolves it via resolveBearerSession.

platformAdminKey.name: x-platform-admin-key
platformAdminKey.description: PLATFORM_ADMIN_API_KEY, compared in constant time. Tenant-bootstrap surface only.

scimBearer.description: Opaque SCIM token compared against a hash in TenantScimToken. Verified in the HANDLER, not at the Edge — the Edge has no database.

lines.description: Register lines REMOVED — hard-deleted, not moved to `SKIPPED`. The count is of rows that no longer exist.

currentVersion.description: The terms version the server is serving. Present ONLY on `terms_version_stale`, absent on `terms_not_accepted`. Re-fetch `GET /api/auth/terms` and present the terms again — do not submit this value back, which would record consent to text the person has not read.

acceptedTerms.description: Must be literally true. Absent or false is 400 terms_not_accepted.

termsVersion.description: The version the client DISPLAYED. Compared for equality with the one being served, so a page left open across a terms change cannot file a consent to a document nobody read.

executions.description: What each decision did when the campaign closed — a REVOKE is applied here, not when it is submitted.

evidenceFileRecordId.description: `null` when the PDF could not be generated or stored. The campaign still closes: the artifact is evidence OF the close rather than a precondition for it, and an operator-triggered regenerate is the follow-up. A client must not read `null` as "the close failed".

counts.description: Derived from `executions`, for callers that do not want to walk the array. `executed + confirmed + skipped` accounts for `total`.

snapshotCount.description: How many subjects were captured. The roster is frozen at creation, so this is the denominator every later count is against — a member who joins or leaves afterwards does not change it.

membershipId.description: `null` once the membership is gone — the FK is `onDelete: SetNull`, deliberately. A campaign must stay readable after a member leaves, and losing the row would destroy the record of what was reviewed.

snapshotRole.description: The role held when the campaign opened, NOT the role now. This is the whole point of a snapshot: the reviewer judges what access existed during the period, and a later change must not rewrite the question.

decision.description: `null` until a verdict is submitted. The count of nulls is what `ACCESS_REVIEW_DECISIONS_PENDING` refuses a close on.

modifiedToRole.description: Set only for a `MODIFY` verdict — the role the subject should hold instead.

executedAt.description: `null` until the campaign closes. A REVOKE is RECORDED when submitted and APPLIED at close, so a non-null value here is the only proof the access actually changed.

AccessReviewDecisionRow.description: One snapshotted subject and the verdict on it, if any.

transitionedToInReview.description: True only when this submission was the FIRST on the campaign and moved it `OPEN` → `IN_REVIEW`. A client can use it to refresh a status badge without re-reading the campaign.

decisions.description: One row per snapshotted subject, ordered by `subjectUserId`. This was a `record` of unknowns with a paragraph explaining why that was acceptable; `openapi-schema-documents-something` refused it, correctly — a schema that accepts anything while describing nothing looks complete to a generated client and is worse than an undocumented route, because the gap is invisible.

lastActivityByUser.description: Subject user id → most recent session activity, or `null` where there is none. Returned with the campaign because it is what a reviewer judges on, and `null` is the answer that matters most: a subject with no activity in the period is the one a revoke is for.

AccessReviewDetail.description: One campaign with the activity a reviewer needs. Shaped for the reviewer page rather than as a normalised record.

outcome.description: What actually happened at close. `EXECUTED` changed access; `NO_CHANGE` is a CONFIRM, which is a decision rather than an action. The three `SKIPPED_*` values are the ones worth reading: `SKIPPED_PENDING` means no verdict was recorded, `SKIPPED_STALE` that the membership changed since the snapshot so the recorded verdict no longer applies to what is there, and `SKIPPED_LAST_OWNER` that applying it would have left the farm with no OWNER. A skip is not a failure — it is the campaign declining to act on a decision it can no longer honour.

AccessReviewExecution.description: What one decision did when the campaign closed.

truncated.description: True when the list hit the shared backfill cap and is a PREFIX rather than the whole set. Newest first, so a truncated page is the most recent campaigns — a client showing a total must not derive it from `rows.length` when this is true.

scope.description: What the campaign covers. A string rather than an enum in the RESPONSE so a campaign created before a scope was renamed stays readable — the accepted request values are a closed set.

status.description: `OPEN` until the first decision is submitted, which transitions it to `IN_REVIEW`; `CLOSED` once closed. A client cannot set this — the first `PUT` of a decision moves it, and `POST /close` ends it.

closedAt.description: `null` until the campaign is closed. Set together with `status: CLOSED`; the two always agree.

reviewerUserId.description: Who must decide. `null` means unassigned — and that is not cosmetic: `ACCESS_REVIEW_NOT_ASSIGNED_REVIEWER` refuses a decision from anyone who is not this person.

_count.description: How many subjects the campaign snapshotted. Returned so a list can show progress without fetching each campaign’s decision graph.

AccessReviewPerson.description: The three fields every person reference on this surface selects. `email` and `name` are nullable because a snapshotted subject may have neither recorded — a reviewer still has to be able to tell them apart, which is why `id` is always present.

wasRequested.description: False when nothing was pending — the call is idempotent rather than an error.

alreadyRequested.description: True when a request was already outstanding; the original date stands.

AccountDeletionRequested.description: The recorded request, with the date the erasure will run.

ActOnNotice.description:
A moderation decision on a notice. The moderator is taken from the verified platform key and is never read from this body; the subject is denormalised from the notice.

`suspendUserId` is REQUIRED when `actionKind` is `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` or `ACCOUNT_TERMINATED`, and rejected as `SUSPEND_TARGET_REQUIRED` otherwise. It is supplied rather than derived for the same reason `recipientUserId` is on a statement: a notice names CONTENT, a reported listing belongs to a farm, and which member to lock out is a judgement rather than a lookup.

id.description: The MEMBERSHIP id — this is what every other operation here takes, not the user id.

role.description: The enum role. A growing union — treat an unrecognised value as the least privilege rather than as an error. When `customRole` is set, THIS field is the base and the custom role overrides it.

customRole.description: Granular overrides on top of `role`. Null for the great majority of members.

status.description: `ACTIVE`, `INVITED` or `DEACTIVATED`. **Load-bearing, not decoration** — this list deliberately includes deactivated members. `REMOVED` never appears: that status exists so the row leaves this list.

applicatorCertNo.description: БАБХ plant-protection applicator certificate. Written by the `certificates` PUT, not by role edits.

provisionedByOrgId.description: Set when the membership came from an organisation provisioning run rather than a manual invite.

activeSessionCount.description: Live sessions for this member. **A best-effort figure: `0` means "none" OR "the session store could not be read".** The read is wrapped so a failure degrades the page rather than failing it, and the degraded value is 0 for every member. Render it as a fact only if that ambiguity is acceptable; prefer showing nothing at 0.

AgDashboardAchievements.description: Every milestone is returned with `earned` false rather than omitted, so a client renders the full set and does not have to know the list. `earnedAt` is null exactly when `earned` is false.

type.description: The journal entry kind, `LogEntryType`. A GROWING union — treat an unrecognised member as a generic entry rather than as an error, or a new kind breaks this widget on a server deploy.

status.description: The task status, `WorkItemStatus`. Note `CANCELED` has one L — `CANCELLED` is a different enum (`CropPlan`). A GROWING union: treat an unrecognised member as active rather than as an error.
Always this value. Switch on it: a 202 is never a token pair and a 200 is never a ticket.

ticket.description: Opaque, single-use, and useless without the `code_verifier` whose challenge you sent. Post it to `POST /api/auth/native/mfa` together with the code.

expiresIn.description: SECONDS the ticket remains valid — a DURATION, not a date. Five minutes, which is time to open an authenticator and read a code. On expiry start sign-in again; a ticket cannot be refreshed.

AppleMfaRequired.description: Sign-in is accepted and INCOMPLETE: the identity token verified, and the farm requires a second factor the app must now collect.

identityToken.description: The JWT from `ASAuthorizationAppleIDCredential.identityToken`. `identity_token` is also accepted.

nonce.description: The RAW nonce this attempt used — the server hashes it. `rawNonce` / `raw_nonce` are also accepted. Single-use.

code_challenge.description:
OPTIONAL, and sending it is how a client DECLARES it can handle a 202. Base64url SHA-256 of a fresh verifier, generated exactly as for `/native/start`; S256 only.

Omit it and a farm requiring a second factor answers `403 MFA_REQUIRED` — which is what every build shipped before this field existed already handles. Send it and that case answers `202` with a ticket instead, so adding the field is opt-in per request rather than a change every client has to absorb at once.

It is also the ticket’s PKCE binding: keep the verifier in memory and send it to `POST /api/auth/native/mfa`. A ticket leaked through a log or a crash report is useless without it. `codeChallenge` is also accepted.

termsPending.description: True when this account has no recorded terms acceptance. Every tenant and person route answers 403 until `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` succeeds.

AppleSignInResponse.description: expiresIn is a DURATION in seconds for the access token; refreshExpiresAt is an ISO INSTANT for the refresh token. The two are deliberately different kinds — do not treat expiresIn as a timestamp.

AssetCreateRequest.description: Payload for creating a tenant agricultural asset (machine, building, equipment). Manufacturer / model / serial / location are free-text; criticality is LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH.

AssetDetail.description: Asset with linked practices and risks. Returned by GET /assets/{id}.

AssetEvidenceLinkRequest.description: Attach a URL as evidence on an asset. File uploads use the multipart /evidence/uploads endpoint with an assetId.

AssetListItem.description: Agricultural asset (machine, building, equipment) as it appears in list views. Criticality is an explicit LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH field.

AssetUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for an agricultural asset. Every field is optional; only provided fields are persisted.

AuditLogEntry.description: A single audit-log row. Hash-chained at the DB layer; this DTO is the read view exposed via the audit/activity endpoints.

password.description: Checked against the password policy and against Have I Been Pwned. The HIBP screen fails OPEN: an outage there must not block signups, so a breached password may occasionally be accepted when the service is unreachable. **No minimum is declared here on purpose** — `validatePasswordPolicy` answers a distinct `too_short`, and a schema-level minimum would collapse that into `invalid_request`.

acceptedTerms.description: Consent to the terms of use and the privacy notice (P3.1). Send `true`. Checked for IDENTITY with `true` rather than truthiness, so no other value satisfies it. Absent or false is `400 terms_not_accepted`, refused before the password is hashed. **Not declared required**, because a schema-level rejection would lose that code — see #1393.

termsVersion.description: The terms version the client DISPLAYED. Compared for equality with the version the server is serving; a mismatch is `400 terms_version_stale`, whose body carries `currentVersion`. This exists so a page left open across a terms change cannot file a consent to a document nobody read — the stored record is of what the person actually saw. Read the current value by rendering `/terms`, or from the `currentVersion` field of a stale refusal.

AuthRegisterStartRequest.description: Registration step 1: creates an UNVERIFIED user and emails a 6-digit code. Every address gets an identical 200, so nothing here reveals whether an account exists. Field constraints are shape-only — the password policy, the HIBP breach check, the Turnstile screen and the consent/version checks all run in the handler and answer with their own error codes.

credentialsFormHidden.description: True means do NOT offer the email/password form. It is a UI instruction, not a capability statement: the Credentials provider stays registered server-side and the backend remains reachable for API clients and tests. A client that reads this as "credentials are disabled" will report the wrong reason when a sign-in fails.

AuthUiConfig.description: Deliberately additive — flags are expected to be added here. Treat an unknown key as ignorable and a missing key as "use the built-in default", never as false.

file.description: The WebP bytes, at most 512 KB.

AvatarUpload.description: multipart/form-data body for an avatar upload. One part, named `file`.

imageUrl.description: The caller’s new effective avatar, as a ROOT-RELATIVE path — the same shape `getCurrentUser` returns for an uploaded photo, so a client can set it straight into the field it already renders.

BlendLotsResult.description: The blend’s outcome. mergeLinks is how many genealogy edges were written, which is what makes the result traceable back to its sources.

alreadyBlocked.description: Whether a block already existed. The action is idempotent — pressing it twice is one row, not an error — so this is how a client tells "nothing changed" from "newly blocked" without a 201/200 split that would confuse a cache.

BlockResult.description: The state of the block after the call.

BottomTabOrder.description: Ordered tenant-relative route suffixes — `/dashboard`, `/farm-tasks`, `/grain/costs`. Validated for SHAPE only: up to 12 unique non-empty strings, never against a list of known tabs, so a tab shipped by a newer client saves against an older server. It is a PREFERENCE, not a grant — resolve it against the surfaces the member may actually reach on EVERY render, because a role can change after the write. `null` and `[]` are different states (see schema).

BriefingAction.description: `field` is null for an action that applies to the whole farm.

skipped.description: How many were left alone — already in the target state, or refused by an invariant (self, or the last active OWNER/ADMIN). A non-zero `skipped` is NOT an error and the operation is still a 200.
How many were left alone — already in the target state, or refused by an invariant (self, or the last active OWNER/ADMIN). A non-zero `skipped` is NOT an error and the operation is still a 200.

CadastreFeatureCollection.description: GeoJSON. EMPTY rather than an error when the cadastre integration is not configured or the viewport holds nothing — a map with no overlay still works.

invalid.description: Normalised lines that failed validation, echoed back.

CadastreImportRequest.description: КАИС identifiers to import. Validated by hand in the handler, NOT by a Zod schema: non-string members are silently filtered out, and an empty result is a 400 carrying the bare `{ error }` body.

enabled.description: Whether КАИС OpenData is configured on this deployment. The upstream URL is NEVER exposed — the client learns only the boolean.

CadastreImportSettings.description: Whether the cadastre-import tab should be offered.

CalculatorBreakEvenFigures.description: Market price against the price that clears cost. covered is null when the comparison cannot be made at all, which is a different claim from false.

CalculatorCashOutLine.description: One currency’s worth of money that actually left the bank.

CalculatorCostSlice.description: One labelled slice of the cost total, composed server-side. labelKey is an i18n key, not a rendered sentence.

CalculatorData.description: The grain net-worth calculator’s whole answer. Every figure is a number, string, boolean or array thereof — no Decimal and no Date crosses this boundary. Read `truncated` before trusting a total: when it is true the figures cover only part of the farm. Read `unallocatedToCrop` too — the per-commodity rows are short by exactly that amount, so a client showing only rows displays a cost that shrinks when the farmer changes how it spreads.

CalculatorExclusionEntry.description: One excluded record, carrying the id a deep link needs and a resolved label.

CalculatorExclusions.description: Every record left OUT of the figures, by class, each naming the id and a label. This is what makes the totals auditable: a farm can see what was not counted rather than wondering why a number looks low.

CalculatorFarmPerArea.description: One currency’s farm-level per-decare rates. TWO denominators, and each figure divides by its own: areaDca is the yield-covered area behind standingValuePerDca and marginPerDca, costAreaDca is the occupied land behind attributableCostPerDca. Display each rate beside ITS denominator — showing the other contradicts it, exactly as on a row (#1512). Value and margin are in `currency` because they follow the row’s price currency; the cost rate is in it because it follows perArea.costCurrency, a DIFFERENT field, so one row can contribute its value here and its cost to another entry. A null currency means the tenant’s display currency, not an absence. marginPerDca excludes any row whose cost rate was refused, so it never blends currencies; `without.marginPerDca` names those.

CalculatorFarmPerAreaFigures.description: The farm’s per-decare answer. `areaDca` is the farm’s LAND — every row’s occupied area, including crops whose rates were all refused — and is currency-independent, so it is deliberately NOT the denominator of anything in byCurrency. Read a rate’s denominator from its own entry.

CalculatorFarmPerAreaOmissions.description: Which commodities each farm rate leaves out, sorted. Compare two lists to say «Без: …» once rather than per figure: when they are equal, one sentence covers the whole block.

CalculatorFarmTotal.description: One currency’s farm-level total. refusedCommodities names what is missing from it, so a total is never quietly short.

CalculatorImputedLandCharge.description: A rent charge imputed for OWNED land, refused with a reason rather than zeroed when the farm has no money lease to observe a rate from.

costAreaDca.description: Decares that `attributableCostPerDca` was divided by — the land the crop OCCUPIES. DIFFERENT from `areaDca`, which is the yield-covered area and is the denominator of the value and margin figures only. Display this one beside the cost rate: showing `areaDca` there contradicts it, and on a farm with no yield estimates `areaDca` is 0 while the cost rate is real.

marginRefusalCode.description: Why `marginPerDca` is null. Non-null exactly when it is null. A UNION of the value and cost vocabularies rather than a list of its own, because a margin needs both sides and is refused for either side’s reason — so there is nothing new to translate. Added in #2259, which fixed a margin that was computed whenever the VALUE figures were, ignoring the cost refusal: a crop with costs in two currencies had `attributableCostPerDca: null` with `COST_CURRENCY_MIXED` and a `marginPerDca` built from that same un-addable sum, reported as `exact`.

costCurrency.description: The currency `attributableCostPerDca` is in. `null` means NO cost row recorded one — render it in the tenant’s display currency, which is what the product already does wherever it prints a cost. Null is an INSTRUCTION, not an absence: a cost that is not in one known currency is withheld rather than labelled, so this is never null beside a non-null rate for any other reason. Do NOT fall back to the market price currency — `attributableCostPerDca` and the market price need not share one, and that is the whole reason this field exists.

costRefusalCode.description: Why `attributableCostPerDca` is null. Non-null exactly when it is null. A SEPARATE vocabulary from `refusalCode`, which describes the value figures: after #1512 the cost rate can be present when they are refused and refused when they are present.

CalculatorPerAreaFigures.description: Per-decare figures over the terms that share a standing-crop area. marginPerDca is a margin over a subset of net worth’s terms, not net worth per decare. It needs BOTH sides: when `costRefusalCode` is set the cost cannot be subtracted, so the margin is withheld too and `marginRefusalCode` says which side failed (#2259).

occupiedAreaHa.description: Hectares the crop OCCUPIES — every parcel it is on (its plantings if a parcel has any, else the parcel itself). NOT `standingCropAreaHa`, which is the area whose expected YIELD is counted and is the denominator for value figures only. Multiply a typed per-decare cost rate by THIS: the other is 0 on a farm with no yield estimates, so the product would be 0.

unattributedCostEntries.description: Cost entries that reached NO commodity, farm-wide. The SECOND reason `cashCostTotal` is a floor rather than a total: an unattributed cost is missing from EVERY per-commodity figure, so the same count rides every row. Non-zero means read the cost — and anything divided by it — as "at least". Distinct from `unallocatedToCrop`, which is land with no crop and is NOT a floor: that spread is deliberately not redistributed, so each commodity’s share stays exact.

CalculatorRow.description: One commodity’s net-worth answer. Figures are accompanied by an uncertainty state rather than presented bare: netUncertainty and costUncertainty say whether a number is exact, a floor, a ceiling, apportioned, partial or refused. A refused net worth carries a CODE to translate and English to fall back to.

CatalogItemDetail.description: A catalogue item as the SINGLE read returns it: nine fields, no defaultUnit relation, and reorderLevel as a NUMBER rather than the list’s decimal string. Carries the БАБХ regulatory fields — quarantinePeriodDays, activeIngredient and pppRegistrationNo — which the farm-record register is generated from.

CatalogItemListRow.description: A catalogue item as the LIST returns it: the raw model, so soft-delete and retention bookkeeping are on the wire too (deletedAt is always null on a listed row). reorderLevel is a decimal STRING here and a NUMBER on the single read — the two operations are not interchangeable.

CatalogItemWriteAck.description: What create and update answer with — the id, name and category ONLY, because both carry a narrow `select`. A client needing the whole item must re-read it.

Contract.description: Grain marketing/supply contract — a forward SALE of produce or PURCHASE of inputs against a counterparty. volumeTonnes/pricePerTonne are decimal strings; terms/pricingNotes are encrypted at rest and returned decrypted. This is the RAW model as create and single-read return it: the soft-delete bookkeeping columns (deletedAt, deletedByUserId, retentionUntil) are on the wire too and are always null on a contract you can read, so they are described here rather than as fields. The LIST endpoint returns this shape plus computed fulfilment/valueAmount/benchmark decorations, which are not part of this schema.

ContractBenchmark.description: Whether this contract is priced above or below market, or why it could not be compared. Deltas are present only when status is OK.

ContractBookTotal.description: One currency slice of the contract book. Buckets are NEVER summed across currencies — 100k EUR plus 100k USD is not 200k of anything — and a contract priced without a currency gets its own bucket rather than joining a neighbour. Sorted by descending value, with the no-currency bucket last.

ContractFulfilment.description: Delivery position of one contract. Tonnages are exact decimal strings. remainingTonnes floors at zero, so over-delivery shows as complete with a full deliveredTonnes rather than a negative remainder.

ContractList.description: A capped page of contracts. `totals` is computed over the rows on this page and filtered to committed statuses, so it is a summary of what was returned — on a truncated page it is NOT the whole book.

ContractListRow.description: A contract as the LIST returns it: the model plus computed fulfilment, value and benchmark. The encrypted terms/pricingNotes are NOT projected on a list — fetch the contract itself for those.

occurredOn.description: The corrected calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Validated by the usecase, which refuses a day that does not exist with `TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID` rather than letting `new Date(string)` resolve it against the server zone.

treatedAreaHa.description: The corrected area for this parcel, in HECTARES. Same convention as the record path: send a whole parcel as its own exact area so the row stays a snapshot, and reserve `null` for a parcel with no recorded area (#2308). Compared at the register’s own resolution.

CorrectDiaryTreatment.description: A correction to a recorded treatment. Every field here is corrected, the parcel list included: `parcels` is the SET, so a parcel absent from it is dropped and one not already on the treatment is added. Two shapes are refused — a list that empties the treatment (`TREATMENT_CORRECTION_WOULD_EMPTY`; that is a withdrawal, which has its own route) and a parcel in a block the treatment never recorded (`TREATMENT_CORRECTION_NEW_BLOCK`). An unchanged list is accepted, so a client may safely send the whole definition back on every save.

occurredOn.description:
The corrected calendar DAY — the commonest mistake, and what this route mostly exists for: work done yesterday recorded today.

Refusals keep the treatments prefix because they are the same parser: a future day is `TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE` and an impossible one such as 2025-02-30 is `TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID`. The prefix is the code’s name, not a claim that this is a treatment.

Moves BOTH the journal entry’s day and the recorded line’s, which the list and the printed record read respectively — leaving one would have two surfaces disagree about when the work happened.

harvestKg.description:
The corrected total in kilograms, for a HARVEST. ONE figure for the activity, never apportioned across parcels.

**`null` CLEARS it** — a weight recorded by mistake has to be removable, and an absent field already means "unchanged", so there would otherwise be no way to say it.

Sent on an activity that is not a HARVEST it is refused with `HARVEST_TOTAL_NOT_APPLICABLE` rather than ignored: a quantity silently dropped is a farmer believing they recorded a yield they did not. The refusal is server-side here, where the record schema does it in a `superRefine`, because this body carries no `kind` to compare against — the stored one decides.

parcelIds.description:
The CORRECTED set of parcels — the whole set, not a delta. Absent means unchanged.

Parcels in this list that the activity does not have are ADDED; ones it has that are missing from this list are DROPPED. Sending the set the definition returned is therefore a no-op, which is what lets an editor submit the whole form back.

**A parcel in a block the activity never covered IS accepted** (owner, 2026-10-26), unlike the treatment correction, which refuses it because the БАБХ register prints one table per block and a new block would appear as its own sheet. Activities are not in that register: the whole-farm «ДНЕВНИК» prints ONE row per activity summing its parcels’ areas, so a new block changes nothing about the document’s shape. The server mints that block’s task.

**Dropping every parcel is refused** with `ACTIVITY_CORRECTION_WOULD_EMPTY`: that is a withdrawal, which has its own route, its own audit event and releases the handle so it stays resumable — none of which a correction does.

parcels.description:
Per-parcel worked area in HECTARES — a REFINEMENT of `parcelIds`, not a replacement, and every `parcelId` here must also appear there. Applies to retained parcels as well as added ones, so a mistyped area is correctable.

**Send a whole parcel as its exact area, not as an omission**: a stored NULL means “the whole parcel” and the diary prints `treatedAreaHa ?? parcel.areaHa`, so omitting it to mean “all of it” and omitting it to mean “unchanged” would be the same request.

Requires `parcelIds`; sent without it the areas would have no set to refine.

CorrectFarmActivity.description: A correction to a recorded field activity. Send `If-Match` with the version from the definition read.

category.description: Which overhead this is the last value for.

incurredOn.description: When it was incurred. Show it — a default from last season should look like one.

payrollHeadcount.description: PAYROLL only. `null` means a plain total was entered, which is NOT the same as zero people.

CostEntry.description: One recorded cost against land, a planting, a season or an inventory item. amount is a JSON number (Decimal converted, absent reads as 0). allocationBasis says WHICH land the cost spreads across and allocationParcelIds is the PARCEL_SUBSET denominator, sorted — except CROP, which spreads across no land at all and instead names its crop in commodityCanonical, superseding the consumption-derived cost for that crop and season. description is encrypted commercial free text returned only on a single read — it is ABSENT rather than null on list rows, which is a different claim from "this entry has no description".

CostEntryBatchResponse.description: Every entry created by one cost sheet, in the order the lines were sent. On a replay of the same Idempotency-Key, the originally created rows — never a second booking.

CostEntryList.description: A capped page of cost entries. When truncated is true rows were DROPPED, so any total computed from rows is wrong — use totalCount.

name.description: The farm name as the farmer writes it, Cyrillic included. The web address is derived from it by transliteration and is NOT this value — read `farm.slug` from the response rather than deriving one.

eik.description: The farm's ЕИК, 9 or 13 digits. OMIT it for «Земеделски стопанин — физическо лице», who has none. Two refusals are specific and worth handling in the form: `EIK_LOOKS_LIKE_EGN` (a personal identity number was typed — say so, do not say "invalid") and `EIK_INVALID` (checksum). Both are decided before the value is hashed or stored, so a number that cannot exist leaves no trace.

CreateFarmRequest.description: Create a farm owned by the caller. The owner is taken from the session and can never be named in the body.

slug.description: Server-generated, transliterated, and carrying a uniqueness suffix. Use it for the redirect; two farms with the same name get different slugs.

identityVerification.description: `not_requested` — no ЕИК was supplied. `pending_review` — a claim was recorded and a human will look at it; this is the value for BOTH a free and an already-taken ЕИК, by design. `deferred` — the farm was created but the claim could not be recorded, so the ЕИК is not yet on file and can be added from farm settings. Never treat `pending_review` as acceptance.

areaScope.description: What the area covers. Absent means "parcel".

risk.description: Snapshot of what the farmer was shown when asking.

CreateInsuranceLeadRequest.description: Send a non-blank `message`, a `quote`, or both — `required` lists `parcelId` only because an either-or cannot be expressed there, and a body with neither is a 400. `quote.coveredParcelCount` is required when `quote.areaScope` is `crop-at-location`. Never send a premium, tariff or instalment amount: there is no such field and one is stripped if present, because the server recomputes the price.

quote.description: Present when the lead carries a quote. Integer cents and basis points, so nothing rounds a float in transit.

CreatedDataStream.description: The create response. ingestToken is the raw credential and appears ONLY here — the server keeps a hash, so it cannot be shown again or recovered.

commodity.description: The CANONICAL commodity, echoed so you know what your spelling resolved to. Named `commodity`, NOT `commodityCanonical` — that is the storage column; this is the resolved value.

category.description: The cost category as entered. Deliberately NOT narrowed to the overhead enum: a crop sheet books the categories a crop actually incurs.

amountPerDca.description: The per-decare rate AS TYPED. `null` means the farmer entered a TOTAL, not that the line is empty — show the row unfilled rather than dropping it, or you hide that the farm has such a cost at all.

currency.description: READ THIS; do not assume the form’s. Bulgaria moved to EUR in 2026 and older rows are BGN, so prefilling the number alone shows a 24 000 лв figure as €24 000 — wrong by the fixed 1.95583 and entirely plausible on screen.

incurredOn.description: Show it, so a stale default looks like one. Every line of one sheet shares this instant — that is what makes them one sheet.

description.description: The row’s NAME — what distinguishes ПРЗ from торове on one sheet. A departure worth stating: list rows elsewhere omit `description` because it is encrypted commercial free text. Returned here only because the rows are the CALLER’S OWN, bounded to one sheet, and without it the sheet comes back as several unlabelled amounts.

CropPlan.description: A sowing plan: one crop, one season, and the succession pattern that generates the plantings. `successions` and `intervalDays` describe the intent; the plantings themselves do not exist until POST /generate is called. _count.plantings is how a client tells a plan that has been generated from one that has not.

CropType.description: A crop the farm grows. commodityCanonical is what joins it to market prices and contract benchmarking; null there is why a contract may get no benchmark. The LIST carries a `_count.varieties`; the create response does not.

CropVariety.description: A variety of a crop type. The spacing, seed-rate, germination and GDD-base columns are Decimal and therefore STRINGS here while the write side takes numbers. soilDefaultsJson holds the curated preferences the soil-suitability verdict compares a parcel against.

avatarUrl.description:
The caller's EFFECTIVE avatar, or `null` for none (draw initials). ONE field for both kinds of avatar: an uploaded photo and an OAuth provider photo both live in `User.image`, so there is no second endpoint to consult and no fallback chain to walk. Read from the database, so it is current the moment an upload lands — fresher than the `picture` claim in a session token, which is minted at sign-in.

**TWO SHAPES, RETURNED AS STORED — the server never absolutises one into the other.** Branch on whether the value starts with `/`:

- a ROOT-RELATIVE path, `/api/account/avatar/{userId}` — an avatar uploaded through this API. Resolve it against the API base and send your session cookie or bearer; it is `getUserAvatar`, and it 404s once the avatar is removed.
- an ABSOLUTE `https://` URL on a THIRD-PARTY host (e.g. `https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/...`) — a provider photo from an OAuth sign-in. Fetch it exactly as given and attach NO credentials.

Both halves of that are failure modes somebody will otherwise hit: resolving an absolute provider URL against the API base 404s, and attaching your bearer token to it leaks the token to that host. Confirmed with the native client (agrent-ios#149): it handles both shapes, and leaving the value as stored is the deliberate choice, because an absolutised URL hides which host is about to be contacted.

May be ABSENT (not just null) from a server older than this field — treat absent as `null`, never as a third state.

deletion.description: A pending account deletion, or `null`. An ABSENT key means the same as `null` — pinned deliberately, so an older server cannot strand a client in a recovery screen it cannot leave. `erasesAt` is `requestedAt` plus the 30-day grace period, derived from the SAME constant the erasure sweep reads, so the date shown and the date the data goes cannot disagree; render it, do not recompute it. Both are ISO instants (`…Z`). Cancel with `DELETE /api/account/deletion` — signing in does NOT cancel, because a background session refresh would then undo a deliberate request. A SUSPENDED caller never sees this field: the route answers 403 first.

platformAdmin.description: Whether this caller is an admin of the PLATFORM tenant — use it to decide whether to render the platform console’s entry (companies, promotions, the daily price override). #1587. **A rendering hint, never a capability:** every platform surface stays gated server-side by `admin.manage` plus a platform-tenant check that answers 404 rather than 403, so a client that forged `true` would see the entry and nothing behind it. It is NOT derived from the `tenant` above — that is the caller’s oldest active membership, which for a superuser who also farms is their own farm, so the flag is resolved against the platform tenant separately. `false` whenever no platform tenant is configured, which is the state in production today.

featureFlags.description: Runtime feature flags, ALREADY RESOLVED for this caller — cohort-gated flags are narrowed server-side, so a client never sees one enabled only for someone else. An ABSENT key means OFF; never treat a missing key as default-on. An EMPTY OBJECT is a legitimate state meaning everything is off, and is what the global kill switch returns. Flags are DB-backed and read at request time, never NEXT_PUBLIC_* (baked in at build time); the server caches the table for 30s, which is the propagation bound for a flip. Re-read rather than caching across sessions.

DataStream.description: A device data stream. The ingest token’s HASH is never projected onto the wire — this shape is what every read returns, and the raw token appears exactly once, in the create response.

DataStreamReading.description: One sensor reading. `unit` is per-reading and may differ from the stream’s declared unit.

valid.description: True when the input is a structurally valid ЕИК: 9 digits with a correct checksum, or 13 digits whose leading 9 are themselves valid. Structure only — it does NOT mean the company exists, is active, or is in the register.

looksLikeEgn.description: True when the input fails as an ЕИК but passes as an ЕГН — both the checksum and a decodable date of birth. Always false when `valid` is true. Use it to change the MESSAGE, not the outcome.

registryName.description:
The registered company name, or null.

**`null` deliberately conflates three different situations** and a client must not distinguish them: no registry provider is configured in this deployment, the provider was asked and had no entry, or the entry carries no name. They are merged because telling an anonymous caller WHICH applies turns this endpoint into a probe for which numbers exist in the register — a distinction worth more to an enumerator than to the form it serves. So render null as "we could not confirm the name", never as "this company does not exist".

EikCheckResult.description: The shape is identical for every outcome — valid, invalid, found, not found. That uniformity IS the control: a response whose size or field set varied with what the register holds would leak the register to anyone willing to iterate.

EmptyBody.description: Empty request body. Used by mutation endpoints whose semantics live entirely in the URL (e.g. POST /restore on a soft-deleted resource).

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

ErrorResponse.description: Canonical error envelope returned by every error path. `code` is a stable string clients can branch on; `message` is human-readable ENGLISH and is a fallback, not UI copy; `params` carries the values a client interpolates into its own translated sentence; `requestId` correlates with server logs; `details` is optional structured context (validation issues, rate-limit info, etc.).

EvidenceCreateRequest.description: Create an evidence record. type=FILE expects a paired multipart upload via /evidence/uploads; type=TEXT/LINK can use this JSON body directly. content is encrypted at rest for TEXT type.

EvidenceDetail.description: Evidence record with the full review history attached. Returned by GET /evidence/{id}.

EvidenceListItem.description: Evidence record as shown in list views. content is encrypted at rest for TEXT type and decrypted transparently on read by the field-encryption middleware.

EvidenceReview.description: A single evidence-review event (submission/approval/rejection) — append-only audit row attached to the evidence record.

EvidenceReviewRequest.description: Lifecycle transition for an evidence record. SUBMITTED is the request-for-review state; APPROVED/REJECTED are reviewer decisions.

EvidenceUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for an evidence record (metadata only — file content is immutable post-upload).

ExchangeInquiry.description: An inquiry against a listing. No inquirer ids ever reach the wire. counterpartyContact and contactSharedAt are a two-sided consent gate rather than ordinary nullable fields: null means consent has not completed, and on a declined inquiry it never will. The listing key is present in the buyer’s outbox and omitted in the seller’s nest — absent, not null.

ExchangeListing.description: A marketplace listing, in the projection every tenant sees. quantityTonnes and pricePerTonne are exact decimal STRINGS — they are quantity and money and must not be parsed as floats. isOwn is computed for the VIEWING tenant, so this projection is not shareable between callers.

ExchangeListingEdit.description: The listing's editable values AS STORED, and the exact body `PUT` accepts. `sellerDisplayName` here is the seller's TYPED alias — NOT the resolved attribution the sibling field carries, which is the farm's verified name when `publishAsFarm` is set. Echoing the resolved value into a full replacement would write a verified farm name into the alias column as literal text. `updatedAt` is a precondition, not a value: `PUT` refuses with LISTING_MODIFIED when it no longer matches.

senderName.description:
The sender's display name (#1348), for every sender in the thread — a colleague at your own farm AND the other party. Null when that user has no name set, so render a fallback rather than an empty bubble label.

It exists because threads are per-PERSON since #1323: a seller can see several threads from one farm and could not tell them apart, and a colleague bubble (`fromMyFarm && !mine`) had no speaker. Owner decision, recorded on #1348.

This does NOT weaken the contact-reveal gate, which gates PHONE and EMAIL — the means of reaching someone off-platform. A name identifies who you are already talking to in a conversation you opened, which is the same disclosure the privacy notice already describes for offer requests.

ExchangeMessage.description:
Use `mine` to decide which side of the thread to render a bubble on. Do NOT compare `senderTenantId` to your own tenant — the server already knows which party is asking and answers for it.

`mine` means SENT BY YOU, the person — not by your farm (#1298). Three speakers are therefore possible on a thread, and a client needs all three: `mine: true` is you; `fromMyFarm: true` is a COLLEAGUE at your own farm (the seller admin answering for the listing's creator) and wants its own speaker label rather than being drawn as either side; both false is the counterparty. `fromMyFarm` is returned rather than derived from the two ids so every client does not reimplement the same comparison.

A deleted message keeps its PLACE: `deleted: true` with a null `body`. Render it as removed rather than dropping it, or the other party's scrollback develops a hole where something they read used to be.

ExchangeMyListing.description: A listing the calling tenant owns, with its inquiries nested. The nested inquiries omit their `listing` key, because this row is it.

ExchangeStatusAck.description: A status transition acknowledgement. Deliberately NOT the full object: the caller already holds it and the transition is the only thing that changed.

ExchangeThread.description:
Private to PEOPLE since #1298. The audience is the thread's principal — the person who opened it on the buyer side, the listing's creator on the seller side — plus any active OWNER/ADMIN of either party farm, so a farm can still answer when the principal is away or has left.

Anyone else gets **404**, including a colleague at a party farm. Not 403: the row is invisible at the database level, so the API cannot tell "not yours" from "does not exist" — and must not, because the difference would leak that a colleague is in a conversation.

`unreadCount` is counted for the CALLER. It used to be per farm, so a colleague opening the thread zeroed everyone's count.

ExchangeThreadSummary.description:
The caller's OWN inbox (#1298) — threads they opened as a buyer, plus threads on listings they created, plus threads on either where they are an OWNER/ADMIN of a party farm. It is no longer the farm's shared inbox, so two colleagues see different lists.

`role` says which side a row is. `hasUnread` is a cheap staleness flag and is now PER PERSON: a colleague reading a thread no longer clears your badge. The exact count needs the thread itself.

A seller may see SEVERAL rows for one buyer farm, because a thread is per (listing, inquirer PERSON). Do not de-duplicate by farm — they are different conversations with different people.

suspendedAt.description: Set when platform moderation has withheld access (P5.9). Included because a person is entitled to know their account is suspended.

ExportedAccount.description: The caller’s own `User` row, decrypted. `emailHash` is deliberately ABSENT: it is a lookup derivation rather than information about the person, and publishing it would hand out the input to a correlation attack against any other system using the same HMAC.

correctedBy.description: The actor’s DISPLAY NAME, resolved per read — not a user id. `null` when the correction was filed by a job with no actor, or the account has since been removed: the record says a correction happened and declines to name someone it cannot name, rather than printing an opaque id into «Коригирано от …».

changedFields.description: Which fields this correction changed — `occurredOn`, `harvestKg`. The request field names, so a client can label the change without parsing prose.

allOf.description:
The WHOLE definition as it stood before this correction, not a diff: a diff needs the reader to already hold the state it was a diff against, and the point of the record is that the state is gone.

**This is the one field that differs from the treatments trail**, which carries a `TreatmentDefinition` here. Everything else in the envelope is identical, and served by the same reader — which is why there are two paths rather than one endpoint answering with either shape.

version.description: The activity’s CURRENT version, so a client holding an older one can tell its trail is stale without a second read.

corrections.description: Newest first, capped at 50. Empty for an activity nobody has corrected — which is what a client should check before showing «Коригирано на …».

version.description: The GROUP’s version, to be sent back as `If-Match` on a correction. `0` for an activity recorded before the group row existed — the backfill starts at 0 rather than claiming a version it never served.

kind.description: The activity. NOT correctable — turning a резитба into a прибиране is a different record, not a correction, which is why the request body has no `kind` field at all.

occurredOn.description: The farm day, from the first completed line. `null` when no line is marked yet, so there is no day to show.

harvestKg.description:
The one total for the activity, in kilograms. `null` on anything that is not a HARVEST, and on a harvest whose total was never recorded or has been cleared.

`null` and `0` are different statements: `0` is a measured harvest of nothing.

parcelCount.description: Register lines under this handle — one per parcel.

lines.description: The recorded parcels. **Correctable**: send the whole corrected set as `parcelIds`, with `parcels[].treatedAreaHa` to refine the areas — including on parcels that were already there, so a mistyped hectare figure is fixable too.

consentedAt.description: When consent was recorded. Moves on each call, because the record that matters is the most recent agreement to the CURRENT wording.

textVersion.description: The version of the consent text that was agreed to, as sent.

hideTagline.description: True when the tagline is WITHHELD from `/f/{handle}` — P6.6. The text is still stored and still returned here; only the public page omits it. Hiding is not deleting: turning the flag off restores the field with nothing retyped.

handle.description: The address the farm now holds, NORMALISED — lower-cased and transliterated from Cyrillic. This is what `/f/{handle}` will serve, and it is often not what was submitted: `Победа` is stored and served as `pobeda`. Show it back to the owner rather than echoing their input, or they will discover the difference from a link that does not work.

normalised.description: True when the stored address differs from the submitted one. Exists so a client can say "your page will be at /f/pobeda" at the moment of choosing instead of after publishing.

reprojected.description: True when the farm was already published and the public page moved as part of this call. The OLD address stops answering immediately — which matters because it may be printed on paper (P6.7) or shared in a chat that cannot be edited.

handle.description: The public address the farm is now served at, as `/f/{handle}` — or `null` when it is not published. A client can use the null to decide whether to show a "view your page" link without re-reading anything.

withdrawn.description: True only when THIS call removed a previously public profile. False on a repeat withdrawal, because there was nothing left to remove — so it reports what happened rather than what the state is.

removedHandle.description: The address that stopped answering, when a withdrawal or a RENAME removed one. A rename returns both: `handle` is the new address and this is the old one, which matters because the old one may be printed on paper (P6.7).

created.description: True when this call CREATED the draft rather than editing one. A client can use it to decide between "saved" and "your public profile has been started" — and it is true exactly once per farm.

reprojected.description: True when the farm was already published and the public page was refreshed as part of this save. False for a draft, because there is no page yet. If this were false on a published farm, the edit would have changed nothing a visitor can see.

state.description: The one-way copy into the farm’s «Agrent» Drive folder. `OFF` means sync was not on when this was uploaded — a SETTING — which is deliberately distinct from `FAILED`, an error an admin can retry. Always `OFF` until the copy job ships.

connected.description: True only when an ENABLED Google connection exists whose granted products include Drive. A calendar-only grant reports false, because it cannot copy a document and offering the toggle would promise a copy that never happens. No account email is reported: the connection record carries granted products and scopes, not an address, and storing one would be a personal-data decision rather than a lookup.

truncated.description: True when the library holds more than one page. The list is newest-first and capped rather than cursor-paginated, and this flag is derived by taking one row more than the cap — not from a separate count, which could disagree with the page it describes.

name.description: The document title. NULL on a tombstone whose bytes were deleted by a person — the name is dropped on a manual delete and KEPT on expiry, because an expiry is the platform acting on a policy and the title is what makes that tombstone readable. Encrypted at rest: a title is routinely «Договор аренда <фамилия>.pdf».

contentType.description: The RESOLVED media type — what the bytes are, not what the upload claimed.

expiresOn.description: The expiry as a calendar DAY KEY (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or null for «Без срок». A day key rather than a timestamp because the concept is a calendar date: lexicographic order is calendar order, and there is no timezone for a reader to get wrong. Computed in Europe/Sofia and fixed at upload from the retention period in force then, so a later settings change never moves it. Named `expiresOn`, not `expiresAt`, because `uploadedAt` and `purgedAt` beside it are INSTANTS and this is a day — one `…At` meaning something different is an exception every client has to remember.

retention.description: The retention period AS IT WAS AT UPLOAD, so a client can say «Пази се 1 година, до …». `expiresOn` alone loses WHY that date was given, and cannot tell a 1-year document from a 2-year one uploaded a year earlier.

purgedAt.description: Set when the bytes were deleted, by expiry or by a person. The ROW SURVIVES: dropping it would make "destroyed by policy on 14 March" and "this never existed" the same observation, which for a compliance register is the worse failure. `/content` answers 404 once this is set.

purgeReason.description: Why the bytes went. EXPLICIT rather than inferable: a client should not have to work out which state a tombstone is in from which fields happen to be null. `name` is dropped on a DELETED tombstone and kept on an EXPIRED one, so null-ness nearly works — and would fail on any row that ever has a null name for another reason.

allOf.description: Who deleted it, for «Изтрит на … от <име>». Null when nobody did: an expiry has no actor, which is the other half of telling the two tombstones apart.

mayDelete.description: Whether THIS caller may delete this document — the uploader, or an administrator. Computed per row and per caller, because a role flag cannot express "may delete their own".

retention.description: The retention period applied to NEW uploads. Changing it never moves an existing document's expiry — every document carries the period it was uploaded under.

driveSync.description: Whether new uploads are copied into the farm’s «Agrent» Drive folder. Turning it OFF stops new copies; it does not revoke the Google connection, which the ДНЕВНИК export still uses, and it does not remove copies already made.

usedBytes.description: Bytes this farm currently holds in the library. The EXACT figure, unlike the bucketed band on `/api/readyz` — this route is authenticated and scoped to the farm that owns the bytes, so a farm learning its own total is not a disclosure. Purged documents stop counting as soon as their bytes go, which is what makes deleting a document free space.

limitBytes.description: The per-tenant ceiling, ALWAYS present — there is no absent-means-unlimited case for a client to handle. Read from an env var rather than the plan: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is absent on this deployment, so every tenant resolves to ENTERPRISE and every ENTERPRISE plan limit is null, meaning a plan-based cap would enforce nothing.

mayEdit.description: Whether THIS caller may change these settings (admin). Readable by every member.

name.description: The farmer's own title for the document. Send this rather than relying on the file part's filename: a Cyrillic name in a multipart part header depends on every parser agreeing about the encoding, while a text field does not. Falls back to the filename when absent or blank, so a web form that sends only `file` keeps working.

eikVerification.description:
What the farmer should be told about their ЕИК:

- `NONE` — no claim has been made. The number shown, if any, predates verification.
- `PENDING` — claimed, waiting for a staff reviewer. Nothing is wrong; nothing is confirmed either.
- `VERIFIED` — a reviewer confirmed the number against the Търговски регистър. This is the only state in which `eik` is authoritative.
- `DISPUTED` — the claim collided with an existing verified claim on the same number.

**`DISPUTED` is not an accusation and must not be worded as one.** It arises from a mistyped digit as readily as from anything else, so render it neutrally and actionably — "does not match an existing record, contact the Agrent team" — never as a suggestion that the farmer misrepresented themselves.

Precedence when a farm has several claims: VERIFIED, then PENDING, then DISPUTED. PENDING outranks DISPUTED deliberately — a farm whose first claim collided and who has since submitted another should see the one in flight, not the dead one.

FarmProfile.description: The one-per-tenant farm identity block printed on the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК. Every field is nullable because the paper form tolerates blanks — an all-null body is the normal answer for a tenant that has not filled it in, not an error. eik/urn are encrypted at rest and returned as plaintext: treat them as sensitive on screen and in logs. There is no egn: the product does not hold a national identity number. sizeHa is a number and grainProduced is an array that is [] rather than null.

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

FarmProfileStaleDataError.description: A 409 `STALE_DATA` from the farm-profile optimistic lock. `error.details` carries `currentVersion` (the stored version) and `expectedVersion` (what you sent). Read them from `error.details`, NOT from the body root — the envelope is nested, and a client that reads the root gets nothing and may then retry with no precondition at all. `currentVersion: 0` means the row does not exist: re-read and retry as a create. It is a conflict to resolve, never a success.

FarmRecordDriveExportRequest.description: The period for exporting a location’s БАБХ ДНЕВНИК to Google Drive. Declared once in `src/lib/schemas/index.ts` and imported by both the route handler and this spec entry, so the two cannot disagree (#1555).

fileId.description: Google’s file id. The only handle for asking Drive what was sent.

fileName.description: The name in Drive, which carries the export DATE and so differs from the download filename. `drive.file` cannot overwrite and Drive permits duplicate names, so without the date a re-export leaves two identically named files and no way to tell which is newer without opening both.

webViewLink.description: Google’s own link to the file, or null when the upload response omitted it.

folderCreated.description: True when THIS export created the folder — the first export, or because the previous folder had been deleted or moved to the bin. Lets the UI explain an apparently empty folder instead of leaving someone to wonder where earlier exports went.

save.description: THE MEDIA TYPE SWITCH. Omitted or false → the response is `application/pdf` bytes. True → it is `application/json` `{ fileRecordId, fileName }` and the PDF is filed in the location’s Farm-records register instead of being returned.

FarmRecordGenerateRequest.description: Generate the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК for a location over a period. Declared once in `src/lib/schemas/index.ts` and imported by both the route handler and this spec entry, so the two cannot disagree (#1555).

auto.description: Generated by the completion job rather than by hand.

missingLabels.description: Bulgarian labels of the FarmProfile / certificate fields still missing — „Земеделски производител", „ЕИК", „сертификат на оператора". A non-blocking nudge, not a validation error.

FarmRecordRegister.description: The location’s generated ДНЕВНИК documents, newest first, plus a completeness nudge.

FarmRecordSaved.description: Where the generated ДНЕВНИК was filed.

farmTaskType.description: A key from the LiteFarm-derived farm-task-type catalog (`src/lib/agriculture/farm-task-types`). An unknown key is a 400 `INVALID_FARM_TASK_TYPE`.

assigneeUserId.description: Assigning fires the existing TASK_ASSIGNED notification.

FarmTaskCreateRequest.description: Create a FARM_TASK. Every id in locationIds/parcelIds/equipmentIds is checked for tenant ownership BEFORE the task is written, so a bad link is a 400 `INVALID_LINK` and never leaves an orphan task. Unknown properties are stripped.

type.description: FARM_TASK or FIELD_OPERATION — the queue merges both.

completedAt.description:
When the work was completed, for «Завършена на …». Set on `RESOLVED` and `CLOSED` only — **`null` for a `CANCELED` task as well as an open one**, so do not render a date merely because the status is terminal (`isCompletedStatus` is deliberately narrower than `isTerminalStatus`, and that gap is the point).

**Do not substitute `updatedAt`.** Any later edit to a closed task moves it, so a task completed in March and re-assigned in September would report September. That is why this field exists rather than a client-side derivation.

Present for historical tasks too: the column has always been written, so a completion date is correct retroactively with no backfill.

parcelIds.description:
Every parcel this task touches — PARCEL task links AND, for a field operation, its operation lines, deduplicated. The same union `GET /tasks/{taskId}/parcels` returns, because a field operation reaches its parcels through its LINES and `?linkedEntityType=PARCEL` would silently omit every planned spray.

Present so a client can count a queue per parcel — the numbers on a MECHANISATOR's whole-farm map — without one request per row on rural LTE (#2474). ALWAYS an array: a task touching no parcel sends `[]`, never an absent field, so a caller need not tell the two apart.

Computed per request rather than cached. Adding a parcel to an existing field operation writes an `OperationParcel` row and no `Task` row, so a task-keyed cache version would not bump and stale ids would be served for the TTL.

mayDelete.description:
Whether THIS caller may delete THIS task — the flag to gate a «Изтрий» control on (#2395). Declared here as well as on `TaskListItem` because BOTH list routes carry it: a client should not have to know which list it is reading to know whether to draw a delete.

Covers all three refusals `DELETE /tasks/{taskId}` can give — `canWrite`, creator-or-admin (`TASK_DELETE_NOT_PERMITTED`), and whether the task is one block’s share of a recorded treatment (`TASK_BELONGS_TO_TREATMENT`, which binds administrators too). See `TaskListItem.mayDelete` for the full reasoning.

**Read it as `mayDelete === false`, never `!mayDelete`**: an absent field is a row cached before it existed, and a stale denial costs a farmer their own task.

FarmTaskListItem.description:
One row of the operator queue. This is the `taskListSelect` projection, NOT the full Task returned by the create — it carries no tenantId, description or metadataJson.

`priority` was previously named here as an omission and is not one: the projection has carried it since the list became orderable by it. It reaches you through `.passthrough()` rather than as a declared field.

FieldBriefingPayload.description: The three `*Configured` / `*Available` booleans exist so a client can say WHY there is no briefing instead of showing an empty card. `aiConfigured` false means the deployment has no model; `satelliteConfigured` false means no Earth Engine credentials; `satelliteAvailable` false means configured but the imagery call did not return. Those are three different messages to a farmer, and `briefing: null` alone cannot tell them apart.

productItemId.description:
An existing product by id. Still fully supported — but the web no longer sends it: the owner removed the product and fertiliser dropdowns on 2026-10-09 in favour of `productName`, because 22 of 24 catalogue items on a seeded farm are archetypes and a picker mostly offered things #1078 refuses at completion.

Send this OR `productName`, never both — an id AND a name for the same kind is `OPERATION_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS`, because preferring one silently would make the other field look honoured and send the operator's typed name nowhere.

**Any category is accepted here, `FERTILIZER` included.** This sentence used to say the opposite — that a fertiliser id is refused with `PRODUCT_EXPECTED` — and it was wrong in both halves (#2362): the permissiveness is deliberate, and `PRODUCT_EXPECTED` is raised by nothing in the server. A liquid fertiliser applied through a sprayer is a legitimate SPRAY, and `prisma/fixtures/ag-demo.ts` files «Aqua Ammonium 28%» exactly that way at 3 L/ha. Refusing it would have refused real agronomy, which is why the owner ruled the rule one-sided on 2026-10-09: the FERTILISER field requires a `FERTILIZER` (`FERTILIZER_EXPECTED`), and the product field requires nothing.

**One exception, and it is not about this field's category but about the KIND.** With `operationType: SEED` the item must be a `SEED`, or the call is refused `SEED_EXPECTED`. That lock exists because #2316 excludes сеитба from the БАБХ register, so without it a real plant-protection product recorded as a sowing would leave the regulated document altogether.

Note that `ParcelDetailSheet.tsx` still filters fertilisers out of its product picker. That is a UI convenience and deliberately NOT enforced here — the picker narrows what is easy to choose, the server refuses only what is incoherent.

productName.description:
A typed product name INSTEAD of `productItemId` — send one or the other, never both. Resolved to the farm's own product of that name (case-insensitive, soft-deleted rows ignored) or created.

**If it has to create one, `newProductRegistration` is required**, because a new product on this path is a PESTICIDE and a ПРЗ without its registration number and quarantine period cannot produce a complete ДНЕВНИК. The refusal is `PESTICIDE_REGULATORY_FIELDS_REQUIRED` and names which field is missing in `params.missing`.

If the name MATCHES an existing product, `newProductRegistration` is ignored — this call creates an operation, not an edit, and an operation payload must not silently rewrite a stored ПРЗ №.

fertilizerItemId.description: An existing fertiliser by id. Still supported; the web now sends `fertilizerName` instead. Send this OR `fertilizerName`, never both. The item MUST be category `FERTILIZER` or the call is refused with `FERTILIZER_EXPECTED` — previously nothing checked this, so a pesticide passed here was filed as a fertilisation.

fertilizerName.description: The fertiliser counterpart of `productName`, with one difference: a fertiliser created this way needs NO regulatory fields. `assertPesticideIsFilable` constrains PESTICIDE only — a fertiliser has no ЗЗР registration and demanding one would invent a rule the product form does not have.

newProductCategory.description:
What a `productName` that matches NOTHING should be created as. Defaults to `PESTICIDE`, which is what a typed spray name usually means.

**Send `FERTILIZER` for a liquid fertiliser applied through a sprayer.** That is a legitimate spray (`FERTILIZER_EXPECTED` is deliberately one-sided), but without this field such a product would be created as a PESTICIDE — and a PESTICIDE cannot be created without a ПРЗ registration number it does not have, so the farmer would be asked to invent one and the item would sit in the wrong category for every later record.

Ignored when the name matches an existing product, and ignored entirely on the `fertilizerName` path, which always creates a `FERTILIZER`.

**Also ignored on a sowing** (`operationType: SEED`), which always creates a `SEED` item. A sowing cannot opt into another category: the register exclusion for сеитба would otherwise let a plant protection product out of the farm record by being recorded as a seed.

newProductRegistration.description: БАБХ fields for a product this call has to CREATE, and only then. Required alongside a `productName` that matches nothing; ignored when it matches. `pppRegistrationNo` makes the trade name in ДНЕВНИК column 4 checkable and `quarantinePeriodDays` feeds column 8 plus the earliest-harvest date in column 9.

FieldOperationCreateRequest.description: Create a spray/field-operation job over selected parcels of a location, assigned to an operator. Applies exactly one input — a product OR a fertilizer — writing one FIELD_OPERATION Task plus one OperationParcel line per parcel.

parcelCount.description: Lines written. `0` is the tell of a PARTIALLY COMMITTED create: the Task exists but has no location link, no operationType and no lines, and nothing can add them afterwards. It is also the discriminator the idempotent-replay check uses, so a replay only short-circuits on a job that really landed.

FieldOperationCreated.description: Identity of the spray job that was created.

location.description: Resolved through the Task↔Location TaskLink. NULL when the job has no location link — which is exactly what a partially-committed create leaves behind, so a null here is a signal, not just an absence.

parcels.description: Every parcel of the linked location (for the map backdrop) — NOT only the parcels this job prescribes. The prescribed set is `lines`. Empty when `location` is null.

done.description: Lines that are DONE **or SKIPPED** — a skip counts as progress.

FieldOperationDetail.description: One spray job: the Task, its per-parcel prescription lines, the linked location with all of its parcels for the map, and a derived progress counter.

comment.description: Sanitised server-side, then reused three ways — Task.resolution (APPROVE only), the audit detail, and the operator notification.

FieldOperationReviewRequest.description: Reviewer decision on a completed field operation. ADMIN-gated, and deliberately separate from evidence review: this finalises the Task.

status.description: APPROVE → RESOLVED; REQUEST_CHANGES → IN_PROGRESS (reopened for rework).

FieldOperationReviewResult.description: The Task status the review moved the job to.

FileReport.description: A DSA Art 16 notice. Used by both the anonymous public form and the signed-in report route; the reporter is taken from the session (or left NULL when anonymous) and is never read from this body.

id.description: A reference for the notice. Returned because Art 16 wants a notifier able to refer to what they filed. It discloses nothing and is not readable back on the public route — there is no GET there, and an anonymous notice stores no reporter, so the reporter read policy can never match it.

status.description: Always `RECEIVED`. The pipeline sets every later state; a client cannot propose one, and this field exists so a notifier sees that the notice was accepted rather than inferring it from the HTTP code alone.

FiledReport.description: Acknowledgement of a filed notice. Deliberately minimal: it does NOT say whether the reported subject exists. A response that distinguished a real id from a made-up one would be an enumeration oracle on an unauthenticated endpoint, so a missing subject is recorded against the moderator-only snapshot instead.

calendarId.description: Google’s id for the «Agrent — Срокове» calendar this farm writes into.

calendarCreated.description: True when THIS run made the calendar — the first sync, or because the farmer had deleted the previous one. Deleting it is the documented way to reset this integration, so a `true` here on an established farm is an ordinary event rather than a fault.

unchanged.description: Events already correct. Counted so a no-op sync is distinguishable from one that did nothing because it failed to read anything.

skippedEdited.description: Events the farmer had edited, left untouched — NOT updated and NOT deleted. Their edit is authoritative: an edited event has been repurposed, so withdrawing it because the original deadline moved on would destroy their work. **Surface this.** A non-zero count means the calendar deliberately disagrees with the farm, and a client reporting a clean sync over it is wrong.

partial.description: True when deletion was SUPPRESSED because the source read was truncated. **Read it.** Creates and updates still ran, but the calendar may hold an event the farm no longer has, and a truncated run is indistinguishable from a complete one without this field.

locale.description: The language the event titles were written in, `bg` or `en`. Fixed when the calendar is created and reused thereafter, so the titles do not change with whichever administrator pressed sync last.

GrainBin.description: A grain bin — a BIN/STORAGE Location with a computed fill. storedTonnes is the bin's HARVESTED_PRODUCE stock converted into tonnes via each lot's unit, so it is comparable to capacityTonnes; fillPct is the fraction of capacity used. Stock in a unit with no tonnage (COUNT/VOLUME) is reported in `unconvertible` and sets `mixedUnits`, which suppresses fillPct rather than being counted at face value.

GrainBinDetail.description: A bin with its stored lots. lotsTruncated is a real truncation marker — a rarity in this API — so a lot count taken from `lots.length` is wrong when it is true; use `lotCount`.

GrainBinWriteAck.description: What create and update answer with. NOT the fill-computed bin — storedTonnes, fillPct and the rest require a read of the stock, so fetch the bin if you need them.

GrainCostRow.description: One row of the grain cost rollup grouped by planting. totalCost = logEntryCost + stockCost. Cost attributed to a planting: journal entries linked to it plus the stock CONSUMED against those entries. An entry covering several plantings is split evenly between them.

GrainDelivery.description: One delivery against a contract. tonnes is an exact decimal string. Deliveries are what `fulfilment` is derived from, so adding or removing one changes the contract’s position.

GrainFieldCostRow.description: Grain cost rolled up to a field, with cost per harvested hectare and per tonne. Same null rules as the season row.

GrainSeasonCostRow.description: Grain cost rolled up to a season, with cost per harvested hectare and per tonne. Per-unit figures are null when the yield register has no area/tonnage for the season, or when the costs span multiple currencies.

state.description: BullMQ job state: waiting, active, completed, failed, …

failedReason.description: ENGLISH free text, and a FALLBACK — not UI copy. It is whatever the worker threw, which is all BullMQ persists about a failure. Render it only when you do not recognise `failedCode`.

failedCode.description:
Stable code for WHY the import failed, for a client that wants to say it in its own language (#1447). NULL unless `state` is `failed`.

Also null when the job DIED rather than refused — and in that case do not show `failedReason`. A refusal names itself with a code, so a null code means the message is whatever the exception carried: «connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379», a stack-trace line, an ORM error. Show your own "something went wrong, try again" copy, as for `SPATIAL_IMPORT_INTERNAL`. `failedReason` is the fallback for a code you do not RECOGNISE — a sentence written for a person — not the fallback for no code at all. (Raised by agrent-ios, who shipped this distinction in their client before the spec said it.)

A boundary upload (`getSpatialImportJob`) sends: `SPATIAL_PARSE_TIMEOUT` (`params.seconds`) when the parse outran its budget; `SPATIAL_TOO_MANY_PARCELS`, `SPATIAL_PARCEL_TOO_COMPLEX` and `SPATIAL_IMPORT_TOO_COMPLEX` (each `params.limit`, plus `params.count` or `params.vertices`) for the complexity caps; `SPATIAL_GEOMETRY_UNPARSEABLE` and `SPATIAL_GEOMETRY_INVALID` (`params.count`) for topology; `SPATIAL_SOURCE_CRS_UNRESOLVED` when a prj-less projected layer could not be placed in Bulgaria; and `SPATIAL_IMPORT_INTERNAL` for a broken server invariant — the one case where the uploader can do nothing but retry, so it carries no params and no detail.

A cadastre import (`getCadastreImportJob`) sends `CADASTRE_GEOMETRY_UNPARSEABLE`, `CADASTRE_GEOMETRY_INVALID` (`params.count`) and `CADASTRE_SOURCE_CRS_UNRESOLVED`. Those three conditions are the same ones the upload path hits, and they are deliberately DIFFERENT codes: nobody uploaded a file, so "fix the geometry and re-upload" is not the remedy. It also sends `CADASTRE_NOT_CONFIGURED` when КАИС OpenData is not configured on the deployment — `GET …/cadastre-import` reports that as `enabled: false` up front, but the POST does not gate on it, so a client that enqueues anyway learns it here — and `CADASTRE_IMPORT_INTERNAL`, the counterpart of `SPATIAL_IMPORT_INTERNAL`.

failedParams.description: The scalars behind `failedCode`, to interpolate into your own sentence — same contract as `ErrorResponse.params`: ids and quantities only, never an object and never personal data. Sizes are raw integer BYTES, not pre-formatted megabytes, so you format them in your own locale. Null when the code needs no values.

ImportJobStatus.description: Poll response for an off-thread import, shared by the boundary-upload and cadastre polls. A not-found or wrong-tenant job answers 404 instead of this shape — the canonical `ErrorResponse` envelope with `IMPORT_JOB_NOT_FOUND` for `getSpatialImportJob`, still a bare `{ error }` body for `getCadastreImportJob`.

IndexTiles.description: A satellite-index overlay source. configured:false means no Earth-Engine credentials on this deployment; configured:true with an EMPTY tileUrl means there is nothing to show (no field geometry, or a transient failure named in error) and the overlay should simply stay off. `date` is the imagery’s real acquisition date and can be older than the date requested, because the composite falls back to the latest available window.
