IngestAck.description: inserted may be LOWER than the batch size — duplicates and out-of-range readings are dropped rather than failing the batch.

IngestReadings.description: A batch of readings plus the stream’s raw ingest token. The batch is bounded server-side (~1000).

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

InquiryAlreadySentError.description: A 409 `LISTING_INTEREST_ALREADY_SENT`. One inquiry per tenant per listing — the `@@unique` index is the guarantee, and a P2002 from it is what raises this. Distinct from `STALE_DATA`: there is no version to re-read and no edit to merge, so a client treating every 409 as a stale edit tells the operator the wrong thing (#1391).

InventoryLedgerEntry.description: One append-only stock movement. UPDATE and DELETE are blocked at the database, so a correction is a NEW opposing entry rather than an edit. entryHash chains the row to its predecessor and is what a tamper check verifies.

InventoryLot.description: An inventory lot of a catalog input (seed / pesticide / fertilizer / …). quantityOnHand is the ledger-derived on-hand quantity in the lot unit; lowStock flags reorder. Cursor-paginate with ?limit=&cursor= for large fields.

InventoryLotDetail.description: A lot with its recent ledger embedded. NOT the same shape as a list row: this has `ledger` and no `lowStock`. For deep history use GET /lots/{lotId}/ledger, which is cursor-paginated.

InventoryLotMoveAck.description: A move acknowledgement. `moved: false` means the lot was already there — the request succeeded and changed nothing, which is different from a failure and different from a move.

InventoryLotPage.description: A cursor page of inventory lots — returned by GET /inventory/lots?limit=&cursor=.

InventoryMovementAck.description: What receive and adjust answer with: the resulting balance and the new chain head. Not the lot and not the ledger entry.

InventoryPageInfo.description: The `{ items, pageInfo }` convention — used by inventory, NOT by grain (`{rows, totalCount, truncated}`) or exchange (`{rows, nextCursor}`). One pager cannot serve all three.

url.description: The acceptance link, token included. The ONLY place the token is returned. Treat it as a credential: do not log it, and do not put it anywhere a URL is recorded.

emailSent.description: **`false` is a real and expected outcome of a 201.** The invite row is committed before the mail is attempted and a mailer failure never fails creation, so a `201 { emailSent: false }` means "the invite exists, nobody was told" — show the admin `url` to pass on by hand.

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

ItemNameConflictError.description:
A 409 from the case-insensitive unique index on `lower(name)`. `error.code` is **`CONFLICT`**, NOT `STALE_DATA` — and that distinction is the point of documenting it.

The other 409 family on this API is the optimistic lock (`STALE_DATA` on the farm profile, a field-operation line, a journal entry), where the remedy is to re-read and retry. **This one is not that.** Re-reading changes nothing: the name is taken and the remedy is a DIFFERENT NAME. A client that treats every 409 as a stale edit will tell the user to reload, which cannot help them.

`error.details` carries Prisma's constraint target — the column list the collision was on — so a form can point at the offending field rather than reporting a generic failure.

The index is on `lower(name)`, so the collision is CASE-INSENSITIVE: «Пшеница» collides with «пшеница», and "Wheat" with "wheat". A client that de-duplicates its own list case-sensitively will think the name is free.

details.description: Per-job payload. For `spatial-import` it carries `tenantId`, `locationId`, `fileRecordId`, `format`, `bounds`, `jobRunId`, `parcelCount` and the reconciliation counts `matched` / `created` / `flagged` — see `SpatialImportDetails`. Other job names carry their own keys.

JobRunEnvelope.description: The worker’s return value once `state` is completed. NULL until then — poll until `state` is `completed` rather than treating a null result as a failure.

JournalFileLink.description: The LINK, not the file. An already-linked file returns its existing link, so this is idempotent per (entry, file).

JournalFileUpload.description: The multipart form. Send `application/json` with `{ fileRecordId, caption? }` instead to attach an already-stored file.

LeasePayment.description: Rent PAID against a lease for one season. `unit` defaults to the lease’s canonical rent unit, which is what stops grain rent being booked against a money obligation. seasonYear is the season settled, which is not necessarily the year in paidAt.

LocationBulkDeleteRequest.description: Declared once in `src/lib/schemas/index.ts` and imported by both the route handler and this spec entry, so the two cannot disagree (#1555).

LocationBulkDeleteResult.description: How many locations were soft-deleted. Ids that do not resolve are SKIPPED, not errors, so `deleted` can be lower than the number you sent — a re-submit deletes 0.

LocationCreateRequest.description: Create a Location (a farm/field block). Parcels are populated by importing a spatial file (shapefile/KML/GeoJSON).

LocationDetail.description: Location with its parcels. Returned by GET /locations/{id}.

boundsJson.description: Bounding box as `[west, south, east, north]` — `[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]`, **longitude first**, per GeoJSON and the reverse of the `lat, lon` a human quotes. WGS84 degrees, exactly four numbers. Null when the location has no imported parcels to bound.

LocationListItem.description: Location as it appears in list views. A Location holds a set of imported Parcels (PostGIS polygons).

LocationListPage.description: The paginated envelope, returned ONLY when `limit` or `cursor` was sent. Note `pageInfo.nextCursor` — the cursor is nested, not at the root.

LocationOperationListItem.description: A FIELD_OPERATION job on this location, resolved through the Task↔Location TaskLink, newest first. `_count.operationParcels` is the number of prescription lines.

bounds.description: Bounding box as `[west, south, east, north]` — `[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]`, **longitude first**, per GeoJSON and the reverse of the `lat, lon` a human quotes. WGS84 degrees, exactly four numbers. Null when no parcel in this location has geometry, which is distinct from an empty box.

LocationParcels.description: A location’s parcels as GeoJSON, with the location’s bounding box.

repeatLast.description: The latest field operation here, regrouped into one repeatable job.

byParcel.description: Last-used product + dose per parcel, keyed by parcel id.

reasonCodes.description: Structured codes — translate these; `reasons` is already-rendered prose.

windows.description: Suitable time ranges REMAINING today (past hours dropped or clipped). Empty means none left today, which the daily `status` alone does not say.

LocationSmartDefaults.description: Pre-fill hints for the spray-job wizard on this location.

LocationUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for a Location. Only provided fields are persisted.

LocationUpdated.description: The update envelope. Deliberately different from the create, which returns the bare Location row with no wrapper.

LogEntryCreateRequest.description: Create a field-journal entry (LogEntry). title is sanitized as plain text; notes is sanitized as rich-text HTML (TipTap). quantities carry the farmOS measure+value+unit lines (an INPUT_APPLICATION entry records the applied amount); locationIds / equipmentIds link the entry to field blocks and equipment. occurredAt defaults to now. plantingLinks record plan-vs-actual: each links the entry to a Planting + lifecycle stage (SOW/TRANSPLANT/HARVEST), writing a LogPlanting row (the entry becomes the ACTUAL for that milestone) and advancing the Planting status. On a HARVEST entry, an optional harvest payload mints a HARVEST_IN inventory lot of the harvested item and records lot genealogy (the input lots consumed on parcelId become DERIVATION parents).

LogEntryFileAttachRequest.description: Attach an already-uploaded FileRecord (photo / document) to a journal entry. Upload the file first via /journal/{id}/files (multipart) or /evidence/uploads, then reference its id here.

LogEntryUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for a field-journal entry. Every field optional. When quantities / locationIds / equipmentIds are supplied they fully REPLACE the existing set (full-replace semantics, matching the create shape).

method.description: `STRAIGHT_LINE` when the tenant has opted in, `NONE` otherwise. `NONE` carries no charges.

yearsElapsed.description: Whole years since purchase, capped at the useful life. **`null` when `purchaseDate` is unset** — what a year costs is knowable without knowing when it started; how much life remains is not.

totalAnnualCharge.description: Sum of `charges[].annualCharge`. `0` when there are none.

reason.description: Why it produced no charge. A growing union — show an unrecognised value as "not depreciated" rather than treating it as an error.

unallocatedCost.description: Sum of `unallocated[].purchaseCost` — the capital value NOT represented in `totalAnnualCharge`.

truncated.description: True when the register hit the read bound, so the totals are partial.

MarketReference.description: The market observation a benchmark was computed against — carried so a client can attribute and date the claim instead of presenting it as an unsourced fact.

kind.description: What this frame is about. A FIELD rather than a named SSE `event:` line, deliberately: a named event is silently dropped by a client that registered no listener for it, so a third kind added later would break older clients invisibly. Switch on this in the default `onmessage` handler and ignore an unrecognised value — visibly, so it can be logged. Both kinds are published; `listing` arrived with the coalesced market tick.

id.description: The row this is about — a notification id (or its dedupeKey) for `notification`. A handle to refetch with, never content. **On a `listing` frame it is not a handle at all:** every tick carries the constant `listings`, because the tick is coalesced across farms and refers to no single row. Refetching it gets nothing.

tenantId.description: Which farm the row belongs to. Present on EVERY kind and never optional — a field present on one kind only would make a client’s handling conditional on the kind. **Its meaning differs by kind, and one reading is a trap:** for `notification` it is the farm whose row this is, and a client belonging to several farms may filter on it before refetching. On a `listing` frame it is **always the constant `listings`** — not a farm, and not displayable: the tick is coalesced across farms, so it has no one seller to name. Never filter on this field for `listing` either way — the exchange browses across all farms, so narrowing to your own memberships would hide every listing worth seeing.

MeStreamEvent.description: The JSON on one `data:` line. IDS ONLY, by design — the row is authoritative and the event is a hint, so a client refetches under its own authorisation rather than rendering what arrived on a broadcast channel.

id.description: The id that was published. Match the `data:` frame on your open stream against THIS value — asserting that something arrived is not the same as asserting your event did.

MeStreamProbeAck.description: The id published to the caller’s own realtime channel. No row was written, so a client that receives it and refetches will find nothing new — the point is the transport, not the content.

slug.description: Use this for navigation. Server-generated and stable.

permissions.description: The coarse permission tier FOR THIS FARM (#1768). Use it to decide whether to render a write control, and nothing else — it is ADVISORY: the server gate is the authority, and a client acting on a stale value is told why by `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE`. It is here rather than only on `GET /api/auth/me` for the same reason `isPlatform` is: that endpoint has no tenant in its path and resolves “the” tenant as the caller’s OLDEST membership, so its `permissions` describe the wrong farm for anyone holding two with different roles — an EDITOR of the farm they have open who was a READER of the farm they joined first is told they cannot write. Derived from this row’s `role`, so it costs no extra query and cannot disagree with it. Read it as optional: an older server omits it.

isPlatform.description: Is this the designated platform farm? (#1587) Offer an admin price console when the OPEN farm’s row has `isPlatform: true` AND its `role` is `OWNER` or `ADMIN`. False for every farm when the deployment names no platform farm, matching the server gate’s fail-closed behaviour. It decides what a client OFFERS and never what is allowed — every platform route still enforces its own gate and 404s outside that farm, so a client that ignored this gets the same refusal it would have got anyway. Read it as optional: an older server omits it, and absent means false. It is deliberately NOT on `GET /api/auth/me` — that endpoint has no tenant in its path and resolves "the" tenant as the caller’s OLDEST membership, so a boolean there would have been false for the owner exactly while they had the platform farm open.

role.description: The caller's role IN THAT FARM: `OWNER`, `ADMIN`, `EDITOR`, `READER`, `AUDITOR` or `MECHANISATOR`. A growing union — treat an unrecognised value as the least privilege rather than as an error.

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier. `codeVerifier` is also accepted.

NativeExchangeRequest.description: One of `code_verifier` / `codeVerifier` is REQUIRED — the schema cannot express "exactly one of" without rejecting the other spelling, so both are optional here and the handler requires one. Sending neither is 400 invalid_grant.

code.description: The six-digit TOTP code. Digits only — anything else answers `MFA_CODE_MALFORMED` and costs no attempt.

code_verifier.description: The verifier whose SHA-256 you sent as `code_challenge` to `signInWithApple`. `codeVerifier` is also accepted. A mismatch answers `MFA_TICKET_INVALID` and does NOT consume the ticket — somebody else holding it must not be able to lock the real user out.

termsPending.description: True when this account has no recorded terms acceptance. Every tenant and person route answers 403 until `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` succeeds.

NativeMfaResponse.description: expiresIn is a DURATION in seconds for the access token; refreshExpiresAt is an ISO INSTANT for the refresh token. The two are deliberately different kinds — do not treat expiresIn as a timestamp.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token from the previous pair. Consumed by this call.
The refresh token for the session to end.

NativeTokenPair.description: expiresIn is a DURATION in seconds for the access token; refreshExpiresAt is an ISO INSTANT for the refresh token. The two are deliberately different kinds — do not treat expiresIn as a timestamp.

tags.description: Stable ASCII slugs, possibly empty, order not significant. IGNORE a slug you do not recognise rather than erroring on it — the vocabulary grows on the server, and a client that threw would break on a deploy it knew nothing about. `GET /trends/news/tags` carries the labels.

NewsItem.description: One aggregated agri-news article. summary and imageUrl are genuinely nullable — many feeds carry neither — so a client must render a headline-only item rather than treating it as malformed.

tags.description: `null` means the reader has NEVER CHOSEN; `[]` means they chose nothing. Both show the full feed, so the difference does not affect filtering — it tells a client whether it may prompt. Do not collapse them: a brand-new reader and one who deliberately cleared their choices want opposite treatment.

NewsPreferences.description: One person’s Новини tag opt-ins. Stored on the server so the same choices apply on web and on every phone, but NEVER applied to the feed implicitly — read them, then pass them to `GET /trends/news?tags=` yourself. The feed is cached under a key shared by every reader, so a server that filtered by the caller’s own preferences would serve one person’s feed to everybody else.

tags.description: Tag keys from `GET /api/t/{tenantSlug}/trends/news/tags`. Order is the reader’s own and is not significant.

NewsPreferencesStored.description: The list as persisted. Never null — a PUT has just written an array, so the "never chose" state of the GET response is not reachable here.

tags.description: Tag keys from `GET /api/t/{tenantSlug}/trends/news/tags`. Order is the reader’s own and is not significant.

NewsPreferencesUpdate.description: Replaces the stored list wholesale. Send `[]` to clear — that is a choice and is stored as one. Duplicates are collapsed.

key.description: Which half of the vocabulary. `crops` are the five commodities; `topics` are subject areas.
Stable ASCII slug. Crop keys are the commodity slugs — the same values `GET /trends/prices` takes — so a tag and a Борса search agree by construction.

labelEn.description: A speakable English label, for iOS Voice Control. A SECOND label, not a localisation mechanism — there is no fallback chain and no third language. Do not prefer it over `label` for display.

Notification.description: One bell notification. title and message are server-authored prose in the producer’s language, NOT translatable keys — a client renders them as given. linkUrl is where the bell navigates and is null when there is no target.

NotificationMarkReadAck.description: Acknowledgement only. The notification itself is not returned — the caller already has it and `read` is the only field that changed.

NotificationStreamEvent.description: The JSON carried by one `data:` line. Narrower than the list row: no tenantId, userId or dedupeKey.

OperationParcel.description: A spray-prescription line of a field-operation job: one parcel, one product, one dose. Marking it DONE deducts dose×area from the FEFO inventory lot and writes an INPUT_APPLICATION journal record.

resolved.description: TRUE when this mark completed the LAST pending line and the job moved to PENDING_REVIEW — not to RESOLVED. It also enqueues the location’s ДНЕВНИК regeneration. Always FALSE on an `alreadyApplied` replay, which is what stops that regeneration running twice for one operator action.

application.description: The inventory + journal effect of COMPLETING a line — non-null only when this write moved the line into DONE from a non-DONE state. `note` says why no stock moved, or (`over_consumption`) that it moved and drove the lot negative. Un-completing does NOT reverse it; the ledger is append-only.

version.description: The line’s version AFTER this write. Send it as the next `If-Match`. On an `alreadyApplied` answer it is the server’s CURRENT version, not the one you expected — sync to it.

alreadyApplied.description: Present only when the version check failed but the line ALREADY carried the status this write wanted. That is a replay of your own success, not a conflict: no second audit row is written and `resolved` is false.

OperationParcelMarkResult.description: Result of marking one prescription line DONE / SKIPPED / PENDING.

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

OperationParcelStaleDataError.description: A 409 `STALE_DATA` from the per-line optimistic lock. `error.details` carries `currentVersion`, `currentStatus` and `expectedVersion` — read them from `error.details`, NOT from the body root, and note this is WIDER than the journal’s stale-data payload. It means someone else changed the line; it is a conflict to resolve (keep-mine / take-server), never a success.

OperationParcelUpdateRequest.description: Operator updates one per-parcel prescription line. The job auto-resolves when every line is DONE or SKIPPED.

truncated.description: True when the server’s cap cut the list. **Read it** — a cut list that does not say so is indistinguishable from a complete one, and the farmer would see a map missing blocks with nothing to indicate it.

geometry.description: Polygon or MultiPolygon in EPSG:4326, lon/lat.

year.description: The newest flight year with imagery over this area, or null when none has. Null is an ORDINARY answer, not a failure — about two thirds of the country is uncovered in any single year.

flightDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, the calendar day **in Bulgaria**. The source stores a local date serialised as UTC (`2023-10-13T21:00:00Z` is midnight in Sofia on the 14th), so this is resolved in `Europe/Sofia` — reading it as UTC reports the flight a day early.

OwnBlock.description: A block the caller MADE. Blocks made AGAINST the caller are never returned, even though the database policy admits both sides of the row — it must, because enforcement runs in the blocked party's context and a row they cannot see cannot refuse them. Hiding them here is what makes a block silent.

reasonCode.description: The category the notifier chose. A string rather than an enum in THIS response on purpose: the accepted request values are a closed set, but a notice filed before a category was renamed must still be readable back, and a codegen client that threw on an unknown value here would break on history.

detail.description: The notifier’s own words, sanitised on the write path. `null` when they wrote nothing — or wrote only markup, which sanitises to nothing and is the same fact to a reader.

status.description: Where the notice is in the pipeline: RECEIVED, TRIAGED, ACTIONED or REJECTED. This is the field the whole reporter-read policy arm exists to deliver — Art 16 entitles a notifier to the outcome. It carries no moderator identity, no rationale and no timing beyond its own row; all of that lives on tables no tenant session can read.

OwnReport.description: A notice as its own reporter may read it back. Every column of the stored row is here, because the policy that admits the reporter is ROW-level and cannot return a subset — which is why nothing may be added to that table without deciding it is reporter-safe.

geometry.description: GeoJSON MultiPolygon in WGS84. Always a MultiPolygon, never a bare `Polygon` — a single-ring parcel arrives as a MultiPolygon containing one polygon.

Parcel.description: One imported parcel polygon. geometry is GeoJSON MultiPolygon in WGS84; areaHa is the on-ellipsoid area in hectares.

areaHa.description: Area in HECTARES as stored, or null when unmeasured.

locationName.description: The block this parcel sits in. Not a convenience: two blocks can each hold a field named «1», so a flat farm-wide list is ambiguous without it.

coordinates.description: Nested coordinate arrays, as GeoJSON nests them. Left unconstrained here rather than modelled to four levels, which no generator handles usefully — the same choice `ParcelGeo` makes.

geometry.description: GeoJSON in WGS84, always SIMPLIFIED for display. Null when the parcel has no outline, which is a normal state — keep the parcel and say it is not drawn, rather than dropping it, so the count still agrees with `parcelCount`.

ParcelByCrop.description: A parcel of one crop, with its block and a display outline.

id.description: Hash of the SORTED member ids, not of the grid cell — so a cluster id in a shared URL resolves to the same parcels, and only changes when the membership genuinely differs.

parcels.description: Every POSITIONED parcel, so the view can switch from clusters to parcels once zoomed in — the cluster grid bottoms out at 200 m and cannot separate them.

bbox.description: Bounding box as `[west, south, east, north]` — `[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]`, **longitude first**, per GeoJSON and the reverse of the `lat, lon` a human quotes. WGS84 degrees, exactly four numbers. Covers the POSITIONED parcels only — a location whose parcels all lack geometry contributes nothing to it.

unpositionedCount.description: Parcels with NULL geometry. Never folded into the total: a holding whose map silently omits 30 fields is data loss the farmer cannot see.

truncated.description: The read hit its 2000-parcel bound; this is a subset.

ParcelClusterOverview.description: Proximity clusters for a location’s parcels, labelled with the nearest settlement.

id.description: Stable across refreshes so a client can key a list on it: the comment’s own id for `COMMENT`, and `resolution:<taskId>` for `RESOLUTION`, which has no row of its own to borrow an id from.

taskKey.description: Nullable because `Task.key` is. Not coerced to a placeholder — an invented key would be indistinguishable from a real one.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601. ONE field for both kinds — the comment’s own time, or the task’s close time for a `RESOLUTION` — so a client sorts and renders a single key. A resolution on a task closed without a terminal status falls back to the task’s `updatedAt`, because a closing note with an approximate time is worth more than a dropped row.

createdBy.description: The same shape `GET /tasks/{taskId}/comments` sends, so a client decodes both with one decoder. Null on a `RESOLUTION`.

ParcelCreateRequest.description: Hand-drawn parcel. `geometry` is a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon in WGS84; rings need ≥4 positions and lon/lat must be in range. A self-intersecting shape is a 400 — PostGIS is the final arbiter, this only catches the common cases early.

areaHa.description: Re-derived server-side from the stored geometry.

ParcelCreated.description: Identity and area of a newly written parcel — NOT the full parcel.

ParcelCropSeason.description: `year` is the HARVEST year. Do not derive it from `sownAt`: wheat sown in October 2025 is the 2026 harvest, so deriving would misfile most autumn cropping by one year. `sownAt` is optional — a back-filled season is often remembered without the drilling date.

cropType.description: The crop VALUE as stored, verbatim and un-normalised. Usually one of the `crops` catalogue values (`Wheat`, `Barley`, `Canola`, `Maize`, `Sunflower`, `Peas`, `Grass`), but NOT guaranteed: `Parcel.cropType` is a free string and a spatial or cadastre import stamps whatever the source file carried. Label it the way the web does — `crops.<value>` when that key exists, the raw value otherwise, never hidden.

parcelCount.description: How many non-deleted parcels carry this crop, farm-wide across every block.

areaHaTotal.description: Total area in HECTARES, summed over those parcels. Null when none of them has a measured area — distinct from 0, which means measured and empty. Convert to дка for display; the server stores hectares.

ParcelCropTotal.description: One crop a farm grows, with its parcel count and area.

ParcelCropTotals.description: Every crop this farm grows. Parcels with NO crop are excluded — "no crop" is not an answer to "which crop did you treat", and such a parcel is still reachable through the per-block list.

areaHa.description: On-ellipsoid hectares, computed in PostGIS. A NUMBER here, unlike the STRING on an OperationParcel line.

coordinates.description: Nested coordinate arrays, as GeoJSON nests them — `[[[lon, lat], …]]` for a Polygon, one level deeper for a MultiPolygon. Left unconstrained here rather than modelled to four levels, which no generator handles usefully.

geometry.description:
GeoJSON geometry, WGS84. Simplified when the read passed `?simplify=` — never for sketch/edit, which needs exact geometry.

**Null is reachable and is not an error.** A simplify tolerance large enough to collapse a small parcel returns null rather than a degenerate shape, so a client must handle a parcel it cannot draw. Re-read without `?simplify=` to get the exact geometry.

cadastralId.description: КАИС identifier `ЕКАТТЕ.масив.парцел`; null when not linked.

soilType.description: Modelled soil label. Null while the async SoilGrids fetch is still pending.

absentFromImportAt.description: When the location’s LAST spatial import did not contain this parcel — it was kept, with all of its history, and marked. Null means it WAS in the last import, or that the location has never been imported into; both mean nothing to warn about. A TIMESTAMP rather than a boolean because "not in the last import" and "not in any import since March" are different facts and only the first is actionable — compare it against the location’s last import.

companyOwners.description: LEGAL-ENTITY owners from the КАИС register, joined at read time on `cadastralId`. Physical persons are never stored, so an individually-owned parcel has an EMPTY array — that is not "unknown owner".

hasActiveLease.description: A non-deleted lease with no end date, or an end date in the future.

ParcelGeo.description: A parcel as the map and the parcel list receive it — geometry as GeoJSON plus the soil and land-administration columns. Wider than the `Parcel` DTO, which describes the `LocationDetail` shape.

ParcelHistoryOperation.description:
A COMPLETED field-operation line for this parcel — the same rows that record a spray or fertiliser application, which is why "linked completed tasks" and "what was applied" are one list and not two. Pending lines are absent: a plan is not history. `doseValue` is a decimal STRING; parsing it as a float rounds the dose.

`title`, `productName` and `doseUnit` are EMPTY STRINGS when their source relation is absent, never null — empty means "not recorded", never "unknown". Filter them out of any concatenation rather than rendering a placeholder.

rentAmount.description: Decimal(14,2) → a JSON STRING, not a number. Parse it before arithmetic.

rentUnit.description: The CANONICAL unit the rent roll groups by — derived from what was sent, not the operator’s literal text.

rentUnitRaw.description: What the operator actually typed, verbatim.

ParcelLease.description: One land-use agreement (аренда/наем) over a parcel.

ParcelLeaseListResponse.description: Leases for one parcel, newest term first, capped at 100. Wrapped in `{ leases }` — the create and update return a BARE lease, unwrapped.

ParcelLeaseRequest.description: Create/update payload for a lease. The same schema serves both, so a PATCH is a FULL replacement: an omitted optional field is written as null, not left alone. Dates are loose strings parsed server-side; an unparseable one becomes null rather than a 400.

ParcelMergeRequest.description: Union ≥2 of the location’s parcels into one new parcel. The originals are SOFT-DELETED and their ids stop resolving — the response carries the new parcel only.

ParcelSplitRequest.description: A GeoJSON LineString blade. It must fully cross the parcel into ≥2 pieces or the request is a 400 and nothing changes.

ParcelSplitResult.description: The pieces the blade cut, each a brand-new parcel.

ParcelUpdateRequest.description: At least one field is required. Sending `geometry` RESHAPES the parcel (area is re-derived and a soil re-fetch is enqueued). Sending an empty `cadastralId` CLEARS the cadastral link; a malformed one is a 400.

ParcelUpdated.description: Area only. There is no `id` and no echoed parcel — re-read the parcel list if you need the updated row.

ParcelWeedObservation.description: `weedKeys` are catalogue Latin binomials and are the reportable half — group and count on these. `otherWeeds` is free text for a species the catalogue does not carry. Render them together; never merge them in storage.

cropType.description: The crop asked for, trimmed — echoed back so a client can match a response to a request.

ParcelsByCrop.description: The parcels of one crop, farm-wide.

expiresAt.description: When the invite stops appearing in this list. There is no `expired` state to observe — see the endpoint description.

inviteDelivery.description: Whether this invite’s email came back undeliverable (#1769). `null` means NOTHING HAS COME BACK, which is not the same as delivered — only invites sent after #1769’s recorder shipped have a correlation row to join a bounce to, and older ones stay null for ever. Otherwise a token derived from the provider’s event: `BOUNCED`, `COMPLAINED`, `FAILED`. **Treat any value you do not recognise as undeliverable of an unknown kind, never as null** — an unrecognised event rendering as “still pending” is the exact bug this field exists to fix.

inviteDeliveryAt.description: When the failure was learned, not when the invite was sent.

PendingInvite.description: A pending invite. Deliberately carries NO acceptance token: the token is a bearer credential and belongs only in the `url` the create response returns (#1450).

PersonBlock.description: The person to block or unblock. The blocker is the authenticated caller and cannot be supplied.

notIncluded.description: Categories deliberately absent, in plain language, because Art 15 is a right to know what is held and a silent omission is a worse answer than a named one.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

contentReports.description: DSA Art 16 notices this person filed. RETAINED through erasure under Art 17(3)(b), which is what makes erasure incomplete — and why they are shown.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

statementsOfReasons.description: Art 17 statements addressed to this person. `actionId` is omitted, so nothing here reaches another party’s moderation record.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

blocksIMade.description: Social blocks this person MADE. Blocks against them are absent — a social block is silent in both directions by design.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeBlocksAgainstMe.description: Commercial blocks against this person. The OPPOSITE of a social block and included, because the exchange already discloses these to them live.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeListings.description: Listings this person created. The listing belongs to the farm; only the authorship column names them.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeInquiries.description: Enquiries this person made, including their own words.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeMessages.description: Messages this person SENT. A counterparty’s replies are somebody else’s words and are absent.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

insuranceLeads.description: Insurance quotes this person requested: the figures they supplied, and the premium they were quoted.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

featureCohorts.description: Dark-launch cohorts this person is in.

PersonalDataExport.description: Every collection is `{ rows, truncated }` and bounded at 1000. The collections present here are derived from one registry the ERASURE also reads, so a column exported but not erased — or erased but never shown — is not reachable.

Planting.description: One succession of a crop plan — the `plantingId` that yield records, cost entries and parcel history refer to. Generated from the plan rather than created directly; the only field a client may update is plannedYieldKgPerHa.

PlantingGdd.description: Growing-degree-day accumulation for one planting. totalGdd is 0 rather than null when there is no weather or no sow date, so a zero is not evidence of anything by itself — check sowDate. targetGdd null means no maturity percentage can be shown.

PlantingSoilSuitability.description: Soil-aware suitability for one planting, comparing the parcel’s modelled soil to the variety’s curated preferences. Advisory only.

PortfolioGrainSummary.description: Org-level grain portfolio rollup: contracted volume (sale/purchase), harvested yield, activity cost and bin storage aggregated across every child farm tenant, with org totals plus a per-tenant breakdown. Each per-tenant figure is computed inside an RLS-bound query against that tenant.

entryCount.description: Rows stored. This import is now the live register.

previousEntryCount.description: Rows in the import this one replaces, or null if it is the first. Returned BESIDE the new count deliberately: an operator who uploads a truncated export sees `entryCount: 40, previousEntryCount: 4100` and knows at once. Without the second number, 40 looks like a success.

skippedRows.description: Rows dropped for having no crop or no product name. A handful is normal — sub-headings and trailing junk. A count near the file length means the binding found the wrong columns, and the register should be re-uploaded rather than trusted.

unparsedDoses.description: Rows whose dose cell held text but no leading number (`по указание на производителя`). The row is KEPT with a null dose — its crop, product, pests and quarantine period are still true — and counted, because this is the number that says the dose column needs a human.

withdrawnCount.description: Entries marked as no longer approved. Kept as rows rather than dropped at import, so a read can state the withdrawal instead of the product simply being absent.

headers.description: The headers the parser bound, in file order. A shape change is visible here.

entryCount.description: What the import recorded at the time it was stored.

storedEntries.description: Rows COUNTED in the table now. Reported separately from `entryCount` on purpose: the two agreeing is the evidence that the snapshot is whole, and returning only the stored figure would make that check circular.

live.description: Null when no import has ever completed — the register is not loaded, and every lookup will miss.

incompleteImports.description: Imports with no `completedAt`. Non-zero means an upload died part-way. Those are invisible to any read by construction, so this is a diagnostic rather than a warning about correctness.

PppRegisterState.description: Which register import is live, and whether it is whole.

file.description: The register as published: `.xlsx`, or delimited text (`.csv`, semicolon, or tab). The parser is chosen from the FILENAME, not the declared content type — `curl -F` sends `application/octet-stream` by default and a browser has three different strings for an `.xlsx`, so here the extension is the more reliable signal. 32 MB ceiling, checked on the declared size before the body is buffered.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, for an `.xlsx` with more than one. Omitted takes the first sheet in workbook order — fine for a single-sheet export, and worth naming otherwise, since "the first one" is not always the one a person means.

PppRegisterUpload.description: multipart/form-data body for a ПРЗ register import.

PracticeCreateRequest.description: Payload for creating a practice. Status defaults to NOT_STARTED. `code` carries the framework reference where one applies (e.g. ISO 27001:2022 A.5.1) and is minted as `CTL-N` for custom practices. Custom practices (isCustom=true) are tenant-specific.

cleared.description: FALSE when there was no live override, which is a 200 and not an error. A superuser clearing an override that was never set has the outcome they wanted, and a client retrying a clear is the normal case.

pointsWithdrawn.description: Points withdrawn from publication. They are NOT deleted — the series and its points are MARKED, so the typed history and the audit trail of what was typed both survive.

entryUnit.description: What to TYPE in, and what the POST will store the value under — `EUR/t` for the nine crops and fertilisers, `EUR/l` for diesel. Surfaced so a client does NOT hold its own copy of that split: the thing being duplicated is a UNIT, and a cross-repo copy has no guard that can see both sides. When two copies disagree the failure is not an error, it is a price wrong by 1000× that renders as a number.

typed.description: The CURRENT run only. `null` after a clear, even though the typed history is kept and the audit row for the clear carries it.

api.description: The feed’s current price, so the form can show what the override is replacing. A hand-entered `manual` price is NOT reported here: it is a typed price too, and presenting it as the API’s would say the override is replacing a feed when it is replacing somebody’s typing.

apiFeed.description: A DIFFERENT claim from `api`, and both are needed. `none` means no feed exists for this commodity EVER — so a typed price is the only source and clearing it leaves nothing, which a client should say before confirming. `api: null` with a real feed means the feed exists but has no current point. One empty column for both would tell the owner their override is replacing something when it is replacing nothing, and would read as a broken feed.

written.description: Points written. Equal to `prices.length` on success, by construction.

handle.description: The farm’s public address. Its page is at `/f/{handle}`.

score.description: Trigram similarity, 0–1. **Zero when browsing** — a request with no `q` has no ranking signal, so every score is 0 rather than a meaningless small number. Do not render it as a relevance percentage; it is a sort key.

QueueStatement.description: A DSA Art 17 statement of reasons, queued for delivery. Stored rendered because what was sent is a fact, and re-rendering later from a changed template would answer a different question.

anonymous.description: Whether the notifier gave an id. **Never which one** — `reporterUserId` is not returned. A moderator decides on the CONTENT, and knowing who reported it invites deciding on the reporter. This flag is returned because it changes whether there is anyone to answer to.

detail.description: The notifier’s own words, sanitised on the write path. `null` when they wrote nothing, or wrote only markup.

snapshot.description: Whether evidence was captured and, if not, why. `SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND` means the content was gone before the capture ran — the normal case for a notice about something real — and `SUBJECT_KIND_NOT_CAPTURABLE` means that surface has no capture path yet. The two are distinct so a deleted listing is not confused with a gap in our own code.

QueuedNotice.description: A notice as the triage queue shows it.

RawErrorResponse.description:
A bare error body: `{"error": "<code-or-message>"}` — NOT the `ErrorResponse` envelope, so there is no `code`, `requestId`, `details` or `params`. Used by the native auth family, where it is the shape RFC 6749 §5.2 specifies for an OAuth token endpoint, and by the cadastre-import job poll. The spatial-import routes used it until #1447 moved them to the envelope. A rate-limit (429) or an unexpected failure (5xx) on the same route still answers with `ErrorResponse`, because the error wrapper builds those rather than the route.

MOSTLY `error` alone, but not a guarantee: `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` adds `currentVersion` on its stale-version branch and declares that with its own `AcceptTermsErrorResponse`. This said "and nothing else" until #1478, which was overstated the day it was written.

kind.description:
Spraying fills the ДНЕВНИК’s химични обработки table; fertilising fills торове. Each carries its own columns, which is why this is a kind rather than a free label.

**`SEED` fills NEITHER** (#2316). Сеитба applies a seed product at a rate, so it belongs on this route rather than `/journal/activities` — the form’s «Продукт» column gets the sown variety. But the БАБХ register covers «РАСТИТЕЛНОЗАЩИТНИ МЕРОПРИЯТИЯ И ТОРЕНЕ» and a sowing is neither, so a SEED row prints in «ДНЕВНИК НА СТОПАНСТВОТО» and is excluded from both БАБХ tables. The per-treatment farm-record refuses for a SEED handle with `NOT_IN_BABH_REGISTER`.

**A SEED record requires a `SEED`-category item** (`SEED_EXPECTED` otherwise). That restriction exists because the exclusion above would otherwise be an escape hatch: a real plant-protection treatment recorded as a sowing would never reach the register. `SPRAY` stays permissive about category because its row still prints.

occurredOn.description: The calendar DAY the treatment happened — a day, not an instant, because that is what the register records and what a farmer knows. It dates both the journal entries and the completed lines. **A future day is refused** (`TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE`), and a day that does not exist, such as 2026-02-31, is refused rather than rolled forward (`TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID`).

parcelIds.description: The parcels treated, as one flat list that may span blocks. The server groups them and writes one field operation per block — the ДНЕВНИК resolves a treatment’s block through the task’s location link, so a single task spanning blocks would print a parcel under a block it was never on. Empty is refused with `TREATMENT_NO_PARCELS`; a parcel of another farm with `REFERENCE_NOT_IN_TENANT` and `params.reference: parcels`, as a 400 rather than a 404 so the refusal does not confirm the row exists somewhere.

treatedAreaHa.description:
The area treated on this parcel, in HECTARES.

**Send a whole parcel as its own exact area, not as an omission.** Owner ruling 2026-10-25 (#2308): the register keeps the area as it was, so a later re-measure of the parcel cannot change an old ДНЕВНИК row. A stored NULL means “the whole parcel” and therefore FOLLOWS the parcel’s current area — which is right for a parcel whose area is unknown and wrong for a historical record of one that is known.

So omit a parcel from this list only when it has no recorded area. This is documented rather than enforced: a NULL is still accepted, because refusing it would break installed builds that send one, and it still prints correctly today.

Compared against the parcel at the register’s own resolution — дка to two decimals — so typing the displayed figure back is accepted and only a difference the document could print is refused with `TREATMENT_AREA_EXCEEDS_PARCEL`.

parcels.description: Per-parcel TREATED area in hectares, for parcels only partly covered (#2072). A REFINEMENT of `parcelIds`, not a replacement: `parcelIds` still says which parcels were treated, and any parcel absent from this list means the WHOLE parcel — which is what the register printed before this field existed. Every `parcelId` here must appear in `parcelIds`, and none may repeat, or the request is refused as a validation error naming the index. Bounded server-side at the parcel’s own area with `TREATMENT_AREA_EXCEEDS_PARCEL`, because only the server holds the parcel row. A parcel whose own `areaHa` is unrecorded has nothing to bound against, so any positive value is accepted and printed for it.

productName.description: A typed product name, resolved to the farm’s own product of that name or created. Send this OR `productItemId`.

pppRegistrationNo.description: ЗЗР рег. № — consulted only when a typed product name has to CREATE a product the farm does not have.

quarantinePeriodDays.description: Карантинен срок in days, AS IT APPLIED ON THE DAY. Stored on each line this treatment records (#1775), so a reprinted ДНЕВНИК shows the waiting period that applied then — and the «най-ранна дата за прибиране» computed from it — even after the product’s own period is later edited. Applies whether the product is one the farm already has or one this call creates; previously it reached only a newly created product’s registration and was dropped for a known product. Omit it and the line stores NULL, which means “not captured” and makes the register fall back to the product — never zero, which would print a waiting period nobody gave. When a typed `productName` has to CREATE a product it ALSO lands on that product’s registration; on a name that MATCHES an existing product the product is not rewritten, because an operation payload must not silently change a stored ЗЗР registration.

phenophase.description: Фенофаза/BBCH — the crop’s growth stage as observed on the day, stored on every line this treatment records (#2072). Free text, because the register’s own column admits a BBCH code OR a Bulgarian stage name and PRZ’s field is free text; an enum would refuse an entry a farmer is entitled to write. Omit it and the line stores NULL, which means “not captured” — never a guessed stage, because this is a regulated document. Accepted on a FERTILIZE record as well as a SPRAY: the line is shared by both kinds and a fertilisation also happens at a growth stage, so refusing it there would need a coded refusal to express something that is not actually wrong. **It does not print in the treatments table, and cannot:** the 12-column «ПРОВЕДЕНИ ХИМИЧНИ ОБРАБОТКИ» table is fixed by заповед РД 11-3194/31.12.2021 and has no phenophase cell. It prints in the separate scouting table, where «Фенофаза/BBCH» is column 2: since #2089 the journal PDF derives one scouting row per treatment line that carries a phenophase, marked with an asterisk and a caption (#1740 Q2). A line with no phenophase still prints as a treatment, it just derives no observation row.

targetNote.description: Вредител — the pest or disease treated.

doseValue.description: Доза на приложение. Per-decare for the register; the unit says which.

applicationTechnique.description: Техника за приложение — one rig per treatment, as the field reality is.

RecordDiaryTreatment.description: A treatment a farmer already carried out. Recorded as DONE — handing work to an operator stays in Задачи.

kind.description:
The activity. Exactly the kinds that apply NOTHING, which is what this route exists for.

Three absences, each deliberate:

`SPRAY` and `FERTILIZE` apply a product and belong on `POST /journal/treatments`, which takes the dose, the ЗЗР registration and the quarantine period this route has nowhere to put.

**`SEED` too** — сеитба applies a seed product at a rate, and always has here: `CreateFieldOperationSchema` admits `SEED` alongside `SPRAY` and `FERTILIZE`, and `ItemCategory.SEED` exists for the varieties. So a sowing goes through the field operation path, where the form’s «Продукт» column gets the sown variety — a cell this route would have left permanently empty. Owner decision 2026-10-25, after agrent-ios spotted that an earlier draft listed `SEED` here while `BARE_ACTIVITY_KINDS` did not, which would have refused every sowing with `OPERATION_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS`.

`OTHER` is absent because existing rows under it carry a product, so admitting it would make one value mean both things.

occurredOn.description:
The calendar DAY the activity happened — ONE day, not a range (owner, 2026-10-25). The template’s «01-05.02.2025» is not carried; an activity spanning several days is dated as one.

Refusals are shared with the treatments route and keep its prefix: a future day is `TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE`, and a day that does not exist such as 2026-02-31 is `TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID` rather than rolled forward. The prefix is historical — the codes describe the DATE, and renaming them would make a client handle two codes for one condition.

parcelIds.description: The parcels worked, as one flat list that may span blocks. The server groups them and writes one field operation per block, for the reason the treatments route documents: the ДНЕВНИК resolves a block through the task’s location link, so one task spanning blocks would print a parcel under a block it was never on.

parcels.description:
Per-parcel worked area in HECTARES, for parcels only partly covered. A REFINEMENT of `parcelIds`, not a replacement, and bounded server-side at the parcel’s own area with `TREATMENT_AREA_EXCEEDS_PARCEL` at the register’s own дка resolution.

**Send a whole parcel as its exact area, not as an omission** — the same rule as treatments (#2308): a stored NULL means “the whole parcel” and therefore FOLLOWS the parcel’s current area, which is right for a parcel whose area is unknown and wrong for a historical record of one that is known. Omit a parcel here only when it has no recorded area.

harvestKg.description:
ONE total for the whole harvest, in kilograms — what the form prints as «Продукция» (owner, 2026-10-25).

**Not per parcel, and not apportioned.** Splitting a measured total across parcels by area would write figures nobody measured into a document a farmer signs. Stored as a single `LogQuantity` on one line’s journal entry, labelled as the activity’s total.

`HARVEST` only. Sent with any other kind it is refused as a validation error rather than ignored, because a quantity silently dropped is a farmer believing they recorded a yield they did not.

title.description: Defaults to the activity name and the block, as the treatments route does.

RecordFarmActivity.description:
A non-chemical activity a farmer already carried out — pruning, cultivation or harvest. Recorded as DONE, like a treatment: handing work to an operator stays in Задачи.

**NOT sowing**, though an earlier draft of this sentence said so. Сеитба applies a seed product at a rate and goes through `POST /journal/treatments` (owner, 2026-10-25) — see `kind`, whose enum has always been the three kinds here.

treatmentGroupId.description: The handle — the request’s `Idempotency-Key` when it sent one.

tasks.description: Field operations written — one per block.

lines.description:
Register lines completed BY THIS CALL — so a replay returns `0`, because nothing remained pending to mark.

**Do not use this as a “did it save” check.** Use `parcelCount`, which is replay-stable. Reading this one that way shows a farmer that nothing saved when everything already had.

parcelCount.description: Total register lines under this handle, whether this call wrote them or a previous one did. Replay-stable, and the same meaning the `parcelCount` on `POST /journal/treatments` carries — which is why it has that name.

harvestQuantityId.description: The `LogQuantity` holding the harvest total, or `null` for any other kind and for a harvest sent without `harvestKg`.

treatmentGroupId.description: The treatment handle. Equals the `Idempotency-Key` you sent; a UUID minted by the server when you sent none.

parcelCount.description: Lines written across every block — the number to show the farmer.

taskIds.description: One per BLOCK, not per parcel. The register joins a block through the task’s location link, so a treatment spanning three blocks is three tasks.

replayed.description: True when this request resolved onto an existing treatment and wrote nothing.

RegisterStartResult.description: Intentionally carries no information about the address. Adding a field here that varied with account state would re-open the enumeration oracle this shape exists to close.

RentRoll.description: Rent by lessor with obligations and payments.

RiskLevel.description: good | watch | stress | unknown. `unknown` means no usable satellite reading, not a failure — render it as absence, never as a fourth severity.

Season.description: A marketing/growing season — the `seasonId` that grain costs, yield records and contracts refer to. startDate and endDate come back as full instants even though they are written as calendar days.

SeasonRecap.description: A season’s headline figures. GROSS and moisture-standardised tonnage are both reported and are not interchangeable; costPerHa is null when nothing carried a cost, which a client must not render as zero.

body.description: The message text. **4000 is measured AFTER sanitising and trimming**, not on what the user typed: the server strips every tag, decodes the canonical entities, trims, and only then checks the length — so padding with markup cannot smuggle a longer message past the limit. **Capping at 4000 client-side is sufficient and conservative.** Sanitising only ever SHORTENS — tags are removed, and `<` becomes `<`, four units to one — so the sanitised length never exceeds the input length. A client that caps cannot be surprised by `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`; that refusal is only reachable by a client that does not cap. The unit is **UTF-16 code units**, not characters and not bytes. For Cyrillic that is 1:1, so a Bulgarian farmer gets 4000 characters. Outside the BMP it is not: an emoji is 2 units, so 2001 emoji is refused at 4002. Counting grapheme clusters over-estimates the allowance; counting bytes under-estimates it. `minLength: 1` is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the surprising part: emptiness is judged after sanitising too. `` is eight characters, satisfies this constraint, sanitises to the empty string, and is refused with `MESSAGE_EMPTY`. A payload can pass the schema and still be rejected as empty. **The server's request validator deliberately permits more (8000).** That is not a contradiction and not a bug: Zod cannot sanitise, so it is a cheap outer bound that rejects absurd payloads, and the real gate is the usecase — which is what keeps `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG` reachable as a CODE rather than collapsing it into a generic validation error. 4000 is the limit a client must respect.

SoilProfile.description: A parcel’s modelled soil profile, fetched asynchronously — null upstream while the fetch is pending, which is an ordinary state rather than an error.

SoilSuitability.description: An ADVISORY verdict. `unknown` is returned whenever the variety has no curated preferences or the parcel has no soil yet — never a fabricated verdict, so a client must render unknown as unknown rather than as a neutral pass.

fileRecordId.description: The staged upload; becomes Location.spatialFileId on success.

SpatialImportAccepted.description: The upload was staged and the parse queued. It has NOT been parsed yet — the parcels are replaced by the worker, so poll the job before refreshing the map.

bounds.description: Bounding box as `[west, south, east, north]` — `[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]`, **longitude first**, per GeoJSON and the reverse of the `lat, lon` a human quotes. WGS84 degrees, exactly four numbers. Null when the import produced no bounded geometry.

SpatialImportDetails.description: The `details` payload of a completed `spatial-import` job. parcelCount is matched + created — what the file contained. flagged counts existing parcels the file omitted, which were kept rather than deleted, so it is deliberately NOT part of parcelCount.

file.description: Shapefile `.zip`, `.kml`/`.kmz`, or `.geojson`/`.json`. The byte cap is enforced on the declared size BEFORE the body is buffered: 5 MB for a shapefile, 10 MB for KML/GeoJSON.

cropType.description: Default crop stamped on every imported parcel. Blank means "mixed / set later".

SpatialImportUpload.description: multipart/form-data body for a parcel-boundary import.

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

StaleDataError.description:
A 409 `STALE_DATA` from the optimistic lock. `error.details.currentVersion` carries the version the server holds — read it from `error.details`, NOT from the body root. A client that treats this as success loses the operator’s edit (#921/#922).

The code is named here because this response had the only 409 in the spec that did not name one (#1391). It explained the semantics and the field to read, and never wrote the literal a client switches on — so the only `code` value visible was this schema's inherited `example: "NOT_FOUND"`, which is a plausible thing to code against and wrong. Four sibling 409s already name theirs in prose exactly like this: see `FarmProfileStaleDataError`, `OperationParcelStaleDataError` and `ItemNameConflictError`.

SuccessResponse.description: Empty success envelope. Returned by mutation endpoints that have no resource to echo back (e.g. status changes, links, deletes).

reason.description:
Why. REQUIRED since #1667 — it becomes the `rationale` of the `ModerationAction` this route records, which is encrypted at rest and is what an Art 17 statement of reasons is composed from. A decision that withholds a farm from a person is not recordable without one.

It was optional and the text was DISCARDED: only `hasReason: true|false` reached the platform audit chain, under a comment correctly saying the rationale belongs on `ModerationAction.rationale` — a row this path never created.

SuspendAccount.description: The account to withhold access from, and WHY. Both required.

resolvedAt.description: **NEVER SENT — there is no such column.** Use `completedAt`. Documented in error; kept only because removing it is a breaking change requiring an API_VERSION bump, which a field that has never been produced does not warrant.

completedAt.description: When the task was completed. THIS is the field the server sends — `resolvedAt` above is documented in error and never arrives. Detail only: the list projection omits it.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

operationType.description: FIELD_OPERATION only: `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED`, `PRUNE`, `CULTIVATE`, `HARVEST` or `OTHER`. Persisted so the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК generator can split химични обработки from торове without re-deriving from the title; legacy rows are null and fall back to a derive-from-title reader. The last three carry no product or dose (#2316) and are what «ДНЕВНИК НА СТОПАНСТВОТО» prints beyond spraying and fertilising. Detail only.

applicationTechnique.description: FIELD_OPERATION only — «Техника за приложение», one rig per job. Detail only.

clientMutationId.description: Offline exactly-once handle. When a FIELD_OPERATION is created from a queued outbox the client's outbox-item id rides in as `Idempotency-Key`; a replayed write dedupes on (tenantId, clientMutationId) and returns the original task. Null for online creates. Detail only.

Task.description:
Unified work-item record covering audit findings, practice gaps, incidents, improvements, and ad-hoc tasks. The type field discriminates which UI surfaces this row appears in.

The full row. `GET /tasks` serves the narrower `TaskListItem`; `GET /tasks/{taskId}` serves `TaskDetail`, which is this plus its relations.

TaskAssignRequest.description: Reassign or unassign a task. Pass null to clear the assignee.

TaskCommentAddRequest.description: Append a comment to a task. body is sanitized server-side (rich-text allowlist) and encrypted at rest (Epic B field-encryption manifest).

TaskCreateRequest.description: Create a task (unified work-item type covering improvements and ad-hoc tasks). The type discriminator gates which UI surfaces this work item appears in.

resolvedAt.description: **NEVER SENT — there is no such column.** Use `completedAt`. Documented in error; kept only because removing it is a breaking change requiring an API_VERSION bump, which a field that has never been produced does not warrant.

completedAt.description: When the task was completed. THIS is the field the server sends — `resolvedAt` above is documented in error and never arrives. Detail only: the list projection omits it.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

operationType.description: FIELD_OPERATION only: `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED`, `PRUNE`, `CULTIVATE`, `HARVEST` or `OTHER`. Persisted so the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК generator can split химични обработки from торове without re-deriving from the title; legacy rows are null and fall back to a derive-from-title reader. The last three carry no product or dose (#2316) and are what «ДНЕВНИК НА СТОПАНСТВОТО» prints beyond spraying and fertilising. Detail only.

applicationTechnique.description: FIELD_OPERATION only — «Техника за приложение», one rig per job. Detail only.

clientMutationId.description: Offline exactly-once handle. When a FIELD_OPERATION is created from a queued outbox the client's outbox-item id rides in as `Idempotency-Key`; a replayed write dedupes on (tenantId, clientMutationId) and returns the original task. Null for online creates. Detail only.

links.description: Edges to other records, newest first. DETAIL ONLY. Also available on its own at `GET /tasks/{taskId}/links`.

watchers.description: DETAIL ONLY. Nothing renders a watcher on either client today — the native app shows `_count.watchers` alone.

_count.description: Relation counts, so a client can badge without fetching the collections. DETAIL ONLY.

label.description: `SLA Breached`, `Triage SLA Breached`, or EMPTY when neither — including for every terminal status. An empty string is the normal case, not a missing value.

sla.description: DERIVED per request from severity + createdAt + status, not a stored column, which is why it is on no model. Added by `getTask`, so DETAIL ONLY.

TaskDetail.description: The task detail. `Task` plus the relations `getById` includes and the `sla` `getTask` derives. `GET /tasks` serves `TaskListItem` instead.

TaskEvidenceLinkRequest.description: Attach a URL as evidence on a task. File uploads use the multipart /evidence/uploads endpoint with a taskId.

entityType.description: What the task is linked TO: `ASSET`, `EVIDENCE`, `FILE`, `LOCATION`, `PARCEL`, `EQUIPMENT` or `PLANTING`. A growing union — treat an unrecognised value as an opaque link rather than an error.

entityId.description: The linked row's id. An id ONLY — nothing about the entity is resolved here.

TaskLink.description: One edge from a task to another record. Ordered newest first.

TaskLinkAddRequest.description: Link a task to another domain entity. The relation field captures semantic intent for downstream traceability views.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

mayDelete.description:
Whether THIS caller may delete THIS task — the flag to gate a «Изтрий» control on (#2395).

Computed server-side because the row cannot answer it: `DELETE /tasks/{taskId}` refuses three cases, and a client has none of the facts for two of them. `canWrite` (a READER sees the list and can delete nothing on it), creator-or-admin (`TASK_DELETE_NOT_PERMITTED`, 403), and whether the task is one block’s share of a recorded treatment (`TASK_BELONGS_TO_TREATMENT`, 409, which binds administrators too).

ONE flag for all three, deliberately — the same choice the journal row’s `mayDelete` makes and for the same reason: a client does not want to know WHICH reason applies, it wants to know whether to draw the control, and an offered «Изтрий» that refuses is worse than an absent one.

**OPTIONAL, and absence is an ordinary state (#2406).** The field is computed after the list cache from two projected columns, and a payload cached by an older projection does not carry them — so rather than report a denial it has no evidence for, the server omits the field. **Read it as `mayDelete === false`, never `!mayDelete`.** An ABSENT field is a row cached before this field existed; treating absence as denial hides the control from the person who created the task. A stale permit costs one refusal, a stale denial costs a farmer their own row.

Advisory, not the control: the route re-checks and answers the codes above. A recorded treatment writes one task per block, so on a farm that records treatments many ordinary-looking rows carry `false` for the 409 reason rather than a permission one.

TaskListItem.description:
One row of `GET /tasks`. A PROJECTION of `Task`, not the whole record — twelve fields matching `taskListSelect`, plus the computed `mayDelete`. Do not decode a list row as a detail row: `description`, `resolution`, `metadataJson`, `reviewer`, `createdBy` and the relations are absent here and present on `TaskDetail`.

`createdByUserId` and `treatmentGroupId` are projected by the server to compute `mayDelete` and are STRIPPED before the response — a list row should not widen what it says about who did what.

name.description: The parcel name as the farmer wrote it. NOT unique — two parcels on one farm may share a name, which is why the response is ordered by name AND id.

geometry.description:
The outline as GeoJSON **MultiPolygon** in WGS84, simplified for display. Always MultiPolygon, never Polygon: the column is `geometry(MultiPolygon, 4326)` and every write path normalises to it, so a client needs no Polygon branch.

**`null` means the parcel has no outline** — a normal state, not an error. Keep the parcel and say it is not drawn rather than dropping it, or your count will disagree with the task. A parcel whose geometry COLLAPSES at the display tolerance falls back to its exact outline rather than arriving as null, so null means exactly one thing.

TaskParcel.description: A parcel linked to a task, for a display-only map. Deliberately status-free: per-parcel operation status lives on the field-operation detail route, so this shape means the same thing whatever the task type is.

TaskParcelsResponse.description: Wrapped in an object rather than returned as a bare array, so a count or a bounds can be added later without a breaking change. The sibling `/links` returns a bare array and is the route that now cannot grow.

TaskSetStatusRequest.description: Lifecycle transition for a task. resolution is required (by convention) when moving to RESOLVED/CLOSED to provide context for the audit trail.

TaskUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for a task. Status changes and assignment go through their own focused endpoints.

user.description: Deliberately NO email — see the DTO docblock.

version.description: Send this back verbatim as `termsVersion`. It is a DATE plus a `-draft` suffix while these terms are unreviewed, and the suffix is deliberate — a stored row reading `…-draft` can never be mistaken for acceptance of a reviewed document. Treat it as an opaque string: do not parse the date, and do not compare versions for ordering.

url.description: The page to show. RELATIVE by design — this product is served on more than one hostname, so an absolute URL would bake in an origin that is right for only one of them. Resolve it against the origin you called.

TermsInfo.description: Carries no body text: open `url` to show the document, so its own draft banner travels with it rather than being restated as a field here.

TraceLotNode.description: One lot in the genealogy graph, annotated with the fields it touched.

TraceLotResult.description: A lot’s provenance in both directions. ancestors and descendants are flat arrays; `edges` is what makes them a graph.

occurredOn.description: The day the work happened as the FARM sees it (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Europe/Sofia), not a UTC slice of `occurredAt`. For a free-hand entry typed between 00:00 and 03:00 in Sofia those two differ by a day.

mayDelete.description: Whether THIS caller may withdraw this treatment — computed server-side so a client can offer «Изтрий» only where pressing it would succeed. It is not a `createdByUserId` field, deliberately: the rule is creator-or-admin AND single authorship, and the second arm refuses admins too, so no field on one row can express it. False on an ordinary manual entry, which has no treatment to withdraw. Advisory, not the control: the route re-checks and answers 403 `TREATMENT_DELETE_NOT_PERMITTED` or 409 `TREATMENT_MIXED_AUTHORSHIP`.

mayCorrect.description:
Whether THIS caller may CORRECT this treatment (#2172) — the flag to gate «Коригирай» on.

**Do not reuse `mayDelete` for this.** The two rules agree today, and they are separate fields because #2280 asks the owner whether to narrow deletion now that a withdrawal is irreversible. If it narrows, a client gating the correction on `mayDelete` would silently hide «Коригирай» from the creators who may still correct — a control missing from the person entitled to it, with nothing failing.

Same two arms as its sibling: creator-or-admin AND single authorship, the second refusing admins too. False on an ordinary manual entry, which has no treatment to correct. Advisory, not the control: the matching `PUT …/definition` re-checks and answers 403 `TREATMENT_EDIT_NOT_PERMITTED` or a 409.

**True for a BARE ACTIVITY too, and this flag does not tell you which route to use.** резитба, обработка на почвата and прибиране are correctable as of #2373, and this flag was always true for them because it is computed from authorship with no condition on the kind — so before that route existed a farmer was told they could correct a pruning while the only correction route refused the handle.

Pick the route on `kind`: an activity goes to `PUT /journal/activities/{treatmentGroupId}/definition`, a treatment to `PUT /journal/treatments/{treatmentGroupId}/definition`. A bare handle sent to the treatment route is refused `NOT_A_TREATMENT`, and the reverse `NOT_AN_ACTIVITY`. So gate the CONTROL on `mayCorrect` and choose the ADDRESS by `kind`.

**Read it as `mayCorrect === false`, never `!mayCorrect`.** An ABSENT field is a row cached before the field existed, and this list reads through a persistent cache; treating absence as denial hides the control from the person who recorded the treatment. A stale permit costs one refusal, a stale denial costs a farmer their own record.

kind.description:
The row’s `FieldOperationType`: `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED`, `PRUNE`, `CULTIVATE`, `HARVEST` or `OTHER`. Widened by #2316 — it read “`SPRAY` or `FERTILIZE`” while the field could already carry the others.

**Switch on this, not on `parcelCount`.** A bare activity — pruning, cultivation, harvest — has parcel lines just as a treatment does, so a client reading `parcelCount > 0` as “this is a treatment” offers correction and the per-treatment PDF on a row with no product or dose to correct, and the correction then refuses with `NOT_A_TREATMENT`.

**The two controls no longer gate on the same kinds.** They did while `SPRAY` and `FERTILIZE` were the only treatments; #2316 added сеитба, which is correctable but not in the register:

| control | kinds |
| --- | --- |
| «Коригирай» — correct the treatment | `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED` |
| «Изтегли PDF» — per-treatment БАБХ extract | `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE` |

Reusing one rule for the other fails in both directions: a farmer is denied a correction they may make on their own sowing, or is offered a register extract the server answers `NOT_IN_BABH_REGISTER` to. Read `mayCorrect` as well for the first — the kind says the record HAS something to correct, `mayCorrect` says this caller may.

`null` is a row whose task predates the column, which the register reads by deriving from the title — treat it as a treatment, because that is all the field operations of that era were.

harvestKg.description:
The harvest’s «Продукция» in kilograms — ONE total for the activity, never apportioned across parcels (agrent-ios #446).

`null` on everything that is not a HARVEST, and on a harvest whose total was never recorded or has been cleared. **`null` and `0` are different statements**: 0 kg is a measured harvest of nothing.

Added because the figure was readable NOWHERE. It lives on a `LogQuantity`, and the only read that returned it — `GET …/activities/{treatmentGroupId}/definition` — is write-gated by design, since its body exists to be edited. So the farmer who recorded a yield could not see it again on the row they recorded it from.

**Derived from the TASK’s `operationType`, not from the quantity’s measure.** `WEIGHT` does not mean produce: a correction to a treatment writes a quantity with the product’s own measure, which is `WEIGHT` for anything sold by the kilogram. Filtering on the measure would report a fertiliser’s APPLIED kilograms as a yield — the same misreading that once printed «Общо за мероприятието» in a column headed «Вид» (#2364).

parcelCount.description:
0 on an ordinary manual entry. The discriminator for “is this a treatment”.

**It counts COMPLETED lines, not all of them.** The figure comes from a query keyed on the journal entries, and a PENDING line has none — the entry is written on completion. So on a partially-written treatment this is smaller than `lineCount`, and the difference is `pendingCount`.

pendingCount.description:
Lines of this treatment still PENDING (#2299). `0` on a finished treatment and on an ordinary manual entry, which has no lines at all.

**Badge on `pendingCount > 0`**, not on `parcelCount !== lineCount` — a free-hand entry has 0 for both and must not read as unfinished.

A partially-written treatment is resumable: re-send `POST …/journal/treatments` with the SAME `Idempotency-Key` and the replay path finishes the remaining lines rather than duplicating the finished ones. `GET …/treatments/{id}/definition` returns everything that request needs. Withdrawing and re-recording also works and is what the farmer had before, but it destroys the lines that did land.

lineCount.description: Every line of this treatment, finished or not. `parcelCount + pendingCount` on a consistent row; carried separately rather than derived so a client never has to infer one of the three from the other two.

totalAreaHa.description: HECTARES, as stored. The web renders decares; the conversion belongs where the number is shown.

doseUnit.description: The unit SYMBOL, not its id.

phenophase.description: Фенофаза/BBCH as captured on the line (#2072). No product fallback — a growth stage is an observation of the crop on a day, so null means not captured and nothing else can supply it. Not printed in the ХИМИЧНИ ОБРАБОТКИ table, which has no such column.

quarantinePeriodDays.description: The line's own period, falling back to the product's.

earliestHarvestOn.description: Computed server-side from the period that applied ON THE DAY, so every client shows the same date and it matches the PDF. Null when no period was captured — never the treatment day itself, which would read as "harvest today".

correctedBy.description:
A DISPLAY NAME, not a user id — this is what «Коригирано от …» prints. Resolved per read rather than stored on the row: a stored name would freeze at correction time, so a later rename would leave the register attributing a correction to a name its owner no longer uses.

`null` when the correction was filed by a job with no actor, or when the account has since been removed. That is deliberate — the record says a correction happened and declines to name someone it cannot name, rather than printing an opaque id at a farmer.
