changedFields.description: Which fields THIS correction changed, by name. A correction that changed nothing files no row at all, so this is never empty.

allOf.description: The WHOLE definition as it stood before this correction, not a diff (owner decision 2026-10-24). A diff needs the reader to already hold the state it was a diff against, and the point of the record is that the state is gone.

version.description: The treatment’s CURRENT version, so a client holding an older one can tell its trail is stale without a second read.

corrections.description: Newest first, capped at 50. Empty for a treatment nobody has corrected — which is what a client should check before showing «Коригирано на …».

version.description: The GROUP’s version, to be sent back as `If-Match` on a correction. From the treatment’s own row (#2172), not from the lines: `OperationParcel.version` is per row and a correction may ADD or DROP a parcel, so there is no stable set of row versions to compare against. `0` for a treatment recorded before the group row existed — the backfill starts at 0 rather than claiming a version it never served.

kind.description:
Which treatment this definition describes. Built from `TREATMENT_KINDS`, the same constant the server maps a stored `operationType` through, so the published members and the ones a response can actually carry cannot drift apart.

`SEED` was missing here until #2316 — and so was the producer, which collapsed a sowing to `SPRAY`, making the two agree with each other and with nothing else. A client that gated «Изтегли PDF» on this field was offered the per-treatment PDF for a сеитба and answered `NOT_IN_BABH_REGISTER`.

`SPRAY` for a task predating the `operationType` column, which is how the register already reads those rows.

occurredOn.description: The farm day, from the first completed line. Null when no line is marked yet.

pppRegistrationNo.description: From the PRODUCT, not the line — it is a property of the registration.

doseUnitSymbol.description:
The dose unit’s SYMBOL, beside its id, because the id cannot be rendered.

It exists for the correction TRAIL. That stores a whole `previous` definition so an inspector can read what a value used to be, and «Беше: 2» is not a dose — a client holding only a cuid can say the dose CHANGED but not what it was.

Carried rather than resolved client-side on purpose: a trail entry is a historical record, and resolving ids against TODAY’s unit catalogue would render a symbol the row never meant if a unit were ever renamed.

waterRateUnitSymbol.description: The water-rate unit’s symbol, on the same terms as `doseUnitSymbol`.

quarantinePeriodDays.description: POINT-IN-TIME. Nothing records what the period WAS when an old line was completed, so this is what was captured then — including nothing. Do not substitute today’s product value: it would make the document authoritative about a number nobody captured.

phenophase.description: POINT-IN-TIME, same reasoning. A plausible guess would make a regulated document authoritative about something nobody observed.

TreatmentDefinition.description: A recorded treatment’s COMPLETE definition, field-for-field re-submittable as the create body. That is the requirement rather than a convenience: a correction replaces the definition, so anything this cannot express is a field a correction would silently drop.

locationId.description:
The block the parcel sits in — the treatment’s fan-out key, and what a client filters a parcel picker by when offering parcels to ADD.

**Not nullable, and it never was in the data.** `Parcel.locationId` is NOT NULL with a required relation to its block, and the record path keys its per-block grouping on it with no null check — which only works because of that: a parcel without a block could not be grouped, so it could not be recorded as a treatment at all. It was declared nullable defensively, and that cost a client a branch it was about to write for a shape the schema forbids.

treatedAreaHa.description: **NULL means the WHOLE parcel**, and it is not an empty value. The register prints `treatedAreaHa ?? parcel.areaHa`, so substituting the parcel area here would turn an absence into a claim — and a correction that round-tripped this prefill would then persist a number nobody typed. Send it back as null to leave it meaning the whole parcel.

parcelCount.description: Lines across every block — planned, not necessarily recorded.

completedCount.description: Of those, how many are DONE. A line gets its ДНЕВНИК entry when it is marked DONE, so this is how much of the treatment the register actually has.

occurredOn.description: The calendar DAY the treatment happened, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Null when nothing has been marked yet — an unmarked line has no date.

complete.description: True only when `completedCount === parcelCount` and at least one line exists. False means partly recorded: retry on the SAME handle and the write finishes the rest.

tags.description: The tags ACTUALLY APPLIED — sorted, de-duplicated, with unrecognised keys dropped. Compare it with what you sent: asking for two tags and getting one back is how you discover that a stored preference has been renamed away. An empty array means the feed is unfiltered.

q.description: The search term applied, or null.

nextCursor.description: Pass back verbatim as `?cursor=` for the next page; null at the end of the feed. OPAQUE — do not parse or construct one. A cursor the server no longer recognises (the 60-day retention deleted its article) is IGNORED and you get the first page, never an error.

TrendNewsResponse.description: The aggregated news feed, newest first. category, tags and q each echo the filter that produced this payload, so a client holding a page can tell a stale response from the one it asked for — which matters more, not less, now that there are three filters to reconcile.

TrendPayload.description: `daysAvailable` can be SMALLER than `daysRequested` — a young tenant has fewer days of history than you asked for. Plot the range you were given, not the one you requested: a chart that pads the difference with zeroes shows a collapse that never happened.

TrendPoint.description: One observation. `date` is a calendar day, not an instant. `count` appears only on listings-derived series, where it is the distinct-tenant sample size — its absence means the series is not sampled, not that the sample was zero.

TrendPricesResponse.description: Market price series for one commodity, grouped by source and region. Staleness is generatedAt minus a series’ lastObservedAt and must be computed against generatedAt rather than the device clock — the payload is cached for 6h and a rural device may be hours off.

source.description: Which feed the quotes came from, e.g. `ec` or `alpha-vantage`. Series from different sources are NOT interchangeable: they quote different stages in different currencies, which is why they arrive as separate series rather than merged.

region.description: A COUNTRY code, not a Bulgarian oblast. Production carries `BG`, `EL`, `RO`, `EU` and — for Alpha Vantage — `GLOBAL`. The oblast codes used by Борса and the parcel registry do not appear here.

stage.description:
The delivery point or market stage WITHIN the region — a feed's own vocabulary rather than ours, so treat it as an opaque label and do not parse it.

It is what distinguishes two series that otherwise look identical: for wheat, the nine Bulgarian delivery points disagree by tens of euros, so a chart that merged them on `(source, region)` alone would average unrelated markets. `region` + `stage` together identify a series.

`National average` is the figure the dashboard prefers, because a farm is not tied to one depot — but not every commodity has one. Wheat, maize and barley do; sunflower's only Bulgarian series is `FGATE`. **Null is normal**, not missing data.

TrendSeries.description: One price line, grouped by (source, region, **stage**) so a chart can split lines that differ in unit, currency or delivery point — BG wheat has nine delivery points whose prices differ by tens of euros per tonne, so two series sharing a source and region are routinely different lines — series are NOT comparable across those without conversion. lastObservedAt is the newest observation anywhere, which is what distinguishes a series reporting this week from one that stopped months ago; both otherwise present a points array whose last entry looks equally current.

Unit.description: A unit of measure from the GLOBAL seeded catalogue — not tenant-scoped, and there is no write path for it. `measure` constrains which units a dose may use; match on `key`, never on the localised `name`.

UnitRef.description: The unit reference embedded in a catalogue item — no `name`, no `createdAt`.

customRoleId.description: `null` UNASSIGNS the custom role. Omitting the field leaves it unchanged — the two are different.

UpdateFarmProfileRequest.description: MERGE SEMANTICS (#1176). Every field is optional and an ABSENT field is LEFT UNCHANGED — only an explicit `null` clears one, and a blank string clears one too. So `{"urn":"123"}` sets `urn` and touches nothing else. `grainProduced` follows the same rule: absent leaves the list alone, while `[]` or `null` clears it. This was NOT the behaviour before #1176, when an omitted field was nulled and a per-field PUT wiped the record — if you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence. A read-modify-write that sends all thirteen fields is still correct and is what the web admin page does; it is simply no longer required. Concurrency: send `If-Match: <version>` to get a precondition — a stale one is a 409 (see below). WITHOUT it, writes are last-write-wins per FIELD: merge semantics already means two admins editing DIFFERENT fields no longer clobber each other, so the precondition closes the narrower SAME-field race rather than the whole lost-update problem. A body that mentions NO field is a true no-op: nothing is written and the version does NOT move, so an empty PUT cannot manufacture a conflict for anyone else. `sizeHa` is a number, bounded at 1,000,000 and refused if negative — and null is not 0: a farm nobody has measured and a farm of zero hectares are different claims. `grainProduced` holds up to 50 strings of at most 120 characters; the server drops blanks and de-duplicates case-insensitively while PRESERVING ORDER, so re-read the response rather than keeping what you sent.

UserRef.description: User identity reference embedded inside other resources (id + display name + optional email).

UserRefShort.description: User identity reference without email — used in audit-log entries and other places where leaking the email would be inappropriate.

YieldRecord.description: Actual harvest production total. tPerHa is computed and not stored — from netTonnesStd when a standardised tonnage exists, otherwise grossTonnes; tPerHaBasis says which, so two t/ha figures are never compared across different bases. valuationNotes is encrypted at rest, returned decrypted, and is absent (not null) on list rows.

YieldRecordList.description: A capped page of yield records. When truncated is true rows were DROPPED, so any total computed from rows is wrong — use totalCount. Note that valuationNotes is absent from these rows by design.

get.description:
Returns a FLAT array by default. With `limit` or `cursor` it returns `{ rows, nextCursor }` and carries a weak ETag (honours `If-None-Match` with 304). With `deleted=true` it returns `{ entries }` and escalates to an admin check. Three bodies on one operation — a client must branch on the query it sent.

**The PAGINATED branch is the ДНЕВНИК and folds one row per treatment (#1740).** A treatment writes one `INPUT_APPLICATION` entry per line — twelve parcels in three blocks is twelve entries — and the register shows ONE row. Each row stays ENTRY-SHAPED, carrying `id`, `type` and `status` at the top level with the treatment detail in an added `treatment` object, so a client that decodes rows as entries keeps working and ignores the extra key. The `id` is a real entry id that `GET /journal/{id}` answers.

`treatment` carries `treatmentGroupId` (the handle), `occurredOn` as a DAY, `kind`, `productName`, `parcelCount`, `totalAreaHa`, `blockNames`, `doseValue` + `doseUnit`, `targetNote`, `applicationTechnique`, `quarantinePeriodDays` and a server-computed `earliestHarvestOn`. An entry belonging to no treatment folds to ITSELF and its `treatment.parcelCount` is 0 — one list, both kinds.

`earliestHarvestOn` is computed from the period captured ON THE DAY (#1775), falling back to the product for lines written before that was stored. Same resolution the ДНЕВНИК PDF uses, so the list and the document cannot disagree about the same number. Null when no period was captured — never the treatment day, which would read as “harvest today”.

**Ordered by `occurredAt` — the day the work HAPPENED — newest first, not by the day the row was typed** (owner ruling 2026-10-14; see #1771). So a back-dated treatment sorts to its own date rather than to the top. The `cursor` for this branch is opaque and encodes `(occurredAt, treatmentGroupId)`: a cursor naming a ROW cannot skip a folded treatment, and one that tried returned 3 treatments as 6 rows. Treat it as opaque and send back exactly what `nextCursor` gave you; a malformed cursor returns the FIRST page rather than a 400, so a stale bookmark is recoverable.

Matches an entry reached by EITHER path: one a person linked to the block explicitly, or one whose operation line sits on a parcel belonging to it. The second path is where the bulk of a ДНЕВНИК lives, because the spray flow writes an operation line and no location link; the second path was added for #1544, before which automatic spray records were absent from a block-filtered journal with nothing to say so.

200.description:
Entries, in one of THREE shapes — the query decides which, and a client that assumes one reads an absent key from another as an empty list rather than as an error.

**Ordering, both branches: `occurredAt` descending — the day the work HAPPENED — with a tiebreak, so the order is TOTAL** (#1771). The paged branch pairs it with `treatmentGroupId` because it folds treatments; the flat branches pair it with `id` because they return rows. `occurredAt` on a diary entry is a DAY, so entries for the same day tie, and the flat read is capped at 200 — without a tiebreak an entry near that cap could appear in one read and not the next with nothing changed.

**Only the paged `{ rows, nextCursor }` shape carries `treatment`** — the folded ДНЕВНИК aggregate (#1832). The bare-array default and the `?deleted=` trash view return rows WITHOUT it, so a client that reads `treatment` must send `limit` to get the paged branch. On that branch the object is ALWAYS present, with `parcelCount: 0` on an ordinary manual entry rather than being absent, so `parcelCount > 0` is the discriminator for "this row stands for a treatment".

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

  The migration is INCOMPLETE and visibly so: a code with no entry yet keeps its English developer-facing sentence, unchanged. There is no flag telling the two apart, which is why switching on `code` and holding your own copy remains the robust choice — the server's `message` is then a better fallback than it used to be rather than something you depend on. Route-level 403s carry their own codes and are described on the operation that returns them.

One route-level code is described HERE rather than per-operation. MOST operations cannot return it — it is confined to the five capability families named below — but it means the same thing on each of them, and one of the five (`upload`) is gated at a choke point that many unrelated routes reach, so an exhaustive per-operation list would be the kind that is wrong by omission:

- `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reachable on any MUTATION outside `/api/auth/**` and `/api/account/**`, which stay open precisely so the way out stays open — `DELETE /api/account/deletion` cancels it, and the person recovers their account and their listings in full. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. The tenant's own ACTIVE exchange listings stay visible to other farms and inbound threads keep arriving — this is the unpaid tenant's own view closing, not a withdrawal.

  The restriction is COMPUTED per request, with no sweep and nothing to settle, so a cleared balance lifts it on the very next request — a client can honestly tell the user to resolve it and refresh. This description deliberately names no remedy beyond that: App Store guideline 3.1.1 keeps the native client from pointing anyone to pay outside the app, so a prescribed destination would be unreachable for one of the two clients (#1490). What both clients CAN do is distinguish this from `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and say which happened.

Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. Each carries `params` so a client composes its own sentence rather than rendering ours (#1679):

- `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. It resets at the start of the next **UTC** month with nothing to settle, so a client can honestly say "next month" — which is what distinguishes it from the one above, where waiting changes nothing. UTC is stated because it is not local: for a Bulgarian user the reset lands at 02:00 or 03:00 on the 1st (EET/EEST), so copy naming a DAY would be wrong for a few hours each month. Raised by agrent-ios, which got this right before the spec said it.
- `AI_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` — the requested model TIER is above this plan's ceiling. Params: `plan`, `tier`, `ceiling`. Distinct from the budget code on purpose: the refusal is on capability, not on spend, so retrying at `ceiling` succeeds immediately and retrying the same tier never will.
- `MODULE_DISABLED` — a product module is off for this tenant. Params: `module` and `reason`. AVAILABLE is a conjunction (plan-allowed AND tenant-enabled) and `reason` says which half failed, because the remedies differ: `"tenant"` means an administrator of THIS farm can turn it on, `"plan"` means the plan does not include it and no administrator can. Do NOT name an administrator without reading `reason` — telling somebody to ask an admin who cannot help is the defect agrent-ios#241 is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph said exactly that. A client that ignores `reason` should stay neutral; the code alone only means "off".
- `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — this deployment runs self-hosted and exposes no in-app checkout at all. Params: `mode`. Nothing the client or the user can do lifts it; do not offer a retry or a plan picker.

  TWO of the five are TRANSLATED by the server (#1677) — `MODULE_DISABLED` and `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — so their `message` is renderable to a user. The other three still carry an English developer-facing sentence: their Bulgarian needs ICU plural agreement, which the server-side renderer does not yet do, and shipping copy that interpolated a wire identifier (`exchange_listing`, `deep`, `FREE`) into a farmer's screen would have been worse than the English. They are tracked on #1677.

  All five carried a legacy `lower_snake:` prefix at the start of `message` until #1677; that prefix is GONE for all of them. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec and your client matches on `plan_limit_exceeded:` or a sibling, switch to `code` — the prefix was removed once the only client depending on it had shipped the codes.

THREE PERMISSION codes are described here, and they are the most diffuse of all of them — 106, 51 and 1 call sites respectively, under most mutating and administrative operations in this document:

- `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing. The remedy is a different role, which only an administrator of that farm can grant, and `params.role` is there so a client can name the role the person actually holds rather than guessing.

  Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only. This one comes from a usecase and means the OPERATION needs write. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this.

  Uncoded until #1767, which is why a client reading a cached copy of this spec should treat its absence as "this server predates the code" rather than "this server cannot refuse a write".

- `ADMIN_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not perform this ADMINISTRATIVE action. Params: `role`. 51 call sites, and it refuses four of the six roles — EDITOR, AUDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR.

  **Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which is a different condition and not a variant of this one.** That one comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only: the whole area is closed to this role. This one comes from a usecase and means the route is NOT admin-only — the caller reached the handler legitimately — and this particular OPERATION needs admin. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this check, so a client that shows one sentence for both will tell an EDITOR they lack access to a screen they are looking at.

  Uncoded until #1779. `ADMIN_REQUIRED` was deliberately NOT renamed to make room for it: that code is one of the four reachable on every route and the most likely of all of them to be live in a shipped client, and a clearer name is not worth a breaking change to it.

- `AUDIT_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role may not perform AUDIT actions. Params: `role`. ONE call site, refusing EDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR. Coded in the same change as its sibling rather than on its own merits: three sibling helpers raising two coded refusals and one bare string is the state that invites a reader to assume the bare one is deliberate.

Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. No tenant route can answer either. They are here because that one function is the choke point all of those routes reach and three of their paths are not in this document yet, so a per-operation list would be wrong by omission:

- `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. A key belongs to a farm and authorises nobody in particular, so this is a category error rather than a permission shortfall: retrying with a wider-scoped key cannot work. Use a user session or a bearer token minted for one.
- `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.
- `TENANT_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED` — the request reached the resolver with neither a slug nor an id. In practice this means a session carrying no tenant, so re-authenticating or picking a farm is the way out rather than retrying. The 404 status is historical and kept on purpose: changing it would break a client that already handles 404 here, and the #1712 migration is about the LANGUAGE a farmer reads.

Both carried an English sentence and no code until #1712. The iOS client resolves display from `error.message` and has no `NOT_FOUND` entry, so an uncoded 404 reached a Bulgarian farmer as English — which is the whole reason these are coded rather than merely translated.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. `max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000))`, so it is never 0 — a client that retries immediately on 0 would spend the next window the moment it opens. The same number is in the body as `retryAfterSeconds`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The preset ceiling for this scope, in requests per window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

post.description: Send `Idempotency-Key` ALWAYS, minted BEFORE the first attempt and reused on every retry of the same logical write. The server maps it to `clientMutationId` under a unique index and returns the ORIGINAL entry on a replay. Minting a fresh key on retry means a response lost after the server committed creates a SECOND record (#924).

201.description: The created entry, or the original one on a replay.

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.

post.summary: Record a treatment already carried out
post.description:
The two-step «Нов запис»: pick a crop, tick parcels, describe one treatment. Recorded as DONE and dated by `occurredOn` — handing work to an operator stays in Задачи.

Send `Idempotency-Key` ALWAYS, minted BEFORE the first attempt and reused on every retry. Here it is also the TREATMENT HANDLE, returned as `treatmentGroupId`: the per-block writes derive their own keys from it, so a replay resolves on the handle rather than on any one of them, and the handle is what later addresses this treatment.

**A reused key RESUMES an unfinished treatment and REPLAYS a finished one.** A replay (`replayed: true`) happens only when every line is already DONE. If the treatment is partly recorded — any failure during marking leaves it so — this request finishes the remaining blocks and lines and answers `replayed: false`. It is safe to re-send: each block carries a derived idempotency key, so an existing block is replayed rather than duplicated, and only lines still pending are marked.

**A reused key is never REFUSED, and the body is not compared** (owner ruling 2026-10-14). Reusing a key whose body differs returns the ORIGINAL treatment with `replayed: true` and writes nothing — the edit is silently not applied. So mint a NEW key the moment a field or the parcel set changes; the server cannot detect that you did not. This matches every other idempotent write in this API (journal entries, the cost batch, exchange messages), none of which compares a body, and it is stated here because the alternative — refusing the reuse — is what a client would reasonably assume.

**The one key that IS refused: an ABANDONED handle, with 410 `TREATMENT_ABANDONED`.** An administrator can abandon a treatment that cannot be finished (`DELETE /journal/treatments/{treatmentGroupId}`, #1777). Its rows are soft-deleted but keep the handle, so this route can tell — and refuses, because a client still retrying a short 201 would otherwise sail past the replay, reach the create path and write the WHOLE treatment again under the same handle, undoing the abandon with nobody seeing it. Found by the agrent-ios session, whose outbox resends such a treatment on every launch. 410 rather than 404 so a client can tell "never landed, write afresh" from "do not send this again"; record the work under a NEW key if it still needs a register entry.

`parcelIds` is ONE flat list that may span blocks — the server groups it and writes one field operation per block, because the register resolves a block through the task’s location link.

No stock is deducted. A treatment is a RECORD of what was applied, and deducting from a lot the farmer may never have tracked would make the inventory wrong in the name of making the diary right (owner ruling 2026-10-13).

Refusals, each a 400 carrying `error.code`: `TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID` (a day that does not exist — 2026-02-31 is refused, never rolled forward to 3 March), `TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE` (you cannot have sprayed tomorrow), `TREATMENT_NO_PARCELS` (an empty `parcelIds`), and `REFERENCE_NOT_IN_TENANT` with `params.reference` naming which list held the stranger — a 400 rather than a 404 so the refusal does not confirm the row exists on some other farm. `params.reference` is `parcels` and nothing else on this route.

A treatment day is the FARM’s day (Europe/Sofia), not the server’s UTC day, so recording today keeps working after local midnight.

`PRODUCT_IS_SAMPLE_ARCHETYPE` — the chosen `productItemId` or `fertilizerItemId` is a SAMPLE product, not a registered one, and the farm record needs a trade name. Refused BEFORE anything is written, so nothing is left behind: the underlying operation write refuses a sample only on the way to DONE, which would leave a partial treatment whose cause repeats on every retry — unfinishable and, with no delete-by-handle yet, unabandonable. Reachable only by id; a typed product NAME never resolves to a sample.

Inherited from the operation write underneath, all 400: `OPERATION_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS` (not exactly one input kind, or an id AND a name for the same kind), `PRODUCT_DOSE_REQUIRED` / `FERTILIZER_DOSE_REQUIRED`, `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` / `FERTILIZER_NOT_FOUND`, `PRODUCT_NAME_REQUIRED` (a name empty once trimmed), `FERTILIZER_EXPECTED` (the fertiliser field was given an item that is not a `FERTILIZER`; **the converse is deliberately NOT enforced** — a liquid fertiliser through a sprayer is a legitimate SPRAY, so the product field accepts any category), `PESTICIDE_REGULATORY_FIELDS_REQUIRED` (a typed name has to CREATE a plant protection product and the ЗЗР registration number or quarantine period is missing — `params.missing` names which), and `DOSE_UNIT_HAS_NO_BASE` (a typed name has to create a product but the dose unit is not a `<base>-per-<area>` rate, so no stock unit can be derived — create the product from the catalogue instead).

Recording a treatment needs WRITE. The restricted machine-operator persona (`MECHANISATOR`) does not have it and is refused 403 — by design: completing work handed to an operator stays in Задачи, and filling in the register is not an operator action.

An earlier version of this paragraph said the journal row’s `mayCorrect` is **false** for these. 201.description: The handle, the counts, and the harvest quantity when one was recorded.

400.description:

Specific to this route: `ACTIVITY_APPLIES_NO_INPUT` if a product or fertiliser reaches the usecase for one of these kinds — refused rather than dropped, because silently ignoring it would file a spraying as a pruning in a regulated record. `HARVEST_NOT_RECORDED` if a harvest total was sent but the completion wrote no journal entry to hang it on, which means the activity itself did not complete; the caller is told rather than receiving a success that recorded no quantity.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

  The migration is INCOMPLETE and visibly so: a code with no entry yet keeps its English developer-facing sentence, unchanged. There is no flag telling the two apart, which is why switching on `code` and holding your own copy remains the robust choice — the server's `message` is then a better fallback than it used to be rather than something you depend on. Route-level 403s carry their own codes and are described on the operation that returns them.

One route-level code is described HERE rather than per-operation. MOST operations cannot return it — it is confined to the five capability families named below — but it means the same thing on each of them, and one of the five (`upload`) is gated at a choke point that many unrelated routes reach, so an exhaustive per-operation list would be the kind that is wrong by omission:

- `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reachable on any MUTATION outside `/api/auth/**` and `/api/account/**`, which stay open precisely so the way out stays open — `DELETE /api/account/deletion` cancels it, and the person recovers their account and their listings in full. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. The tenant's own ACTIVE exchange listings stay visible to other farms and inbound threads keep arriving — this is the unpaid tenant's own view closing, not a withdrawal.

  The restriction is COMPUTED per request, with no sweep and nothing to settle, so a cleared balance lifts it on the very next request — a client can honestly tell the user to resolve it and refresh. This description deliberately names no remedy beyond that: App Store guideline 3.1.1 keeps the native client from pointing anyone to pay outside the app, so a prescribed destination would be unreachable for one of the two clients (#1490). What both clients CAN do is distinguish this from `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and say which happened.

Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. Each carries `params` so a client composes its own sentence rather than rendering ours (#1679):

- `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. It resets at the start of the next **UTC** month with nothing to settle, so a client can honestly say "next month" — which is what distinguishes it from the one above, where waiting changes nothing. UTC is stated because it is not local: for a Bulgarian user the reset lands at 02:00 or 03:00 on the 1st (EET/EEST), so copy naming a DAY would be wrong for a few hours each month. Raised by agrent-ios, which got this right before the spec said it.
- `AI_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` — the requested model TIER is above this plan's ceiling. Params: `plan`, `tier`, `ceiling`. Distinct from the budget code on purpose: the refusal is on capability, not on spend, so retrying at `ceiling` succeeds immediately and retrying the same tier never will.
- `MODULE_DISABLED` — a product module is off for this tenant. Params: `module` and `reason`. AVAILABLE is a conjunction (plan-allowed AND tenant-enabled) and `reason` says which half failed, because the remedies differ: `"tenant"` means an administrator of THIS farm can turn it on, `"plan"` means the plan does not include it and no administrator can. Do NOT name an administrator without reading `reason` — telling somebody to ask an admin who cannot help is the defect agrent-ios#241 is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph said exactly that. A client that ignores `reason` should stay neutral; the code alone only means "off".
- `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — this deployment runs self-hosted and exposes no in-app checkout at all. Params: `mode`. Nothing the client or the user can do lifts it; do not offer a retry or a plan picker.

  TWO of the five are TRANSLATED by the server (#1677) — `MODULE_DISABLED` and `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — so their `message` is renderable to a user. The other three still carry an English developer-facing sentence: their Bulgarian needs ICU plural agreement, which the server-side renderer does not yet do, and shipping copy that interpolated a wire identifier (`exchange_listing`, `deep`, `FREE`) into a farmer's screen would have been worse than the English. They are tracked on #1677.

  All five carried a legacy `lower_snake:` prefix at the start of `message` until #1677; that prefix is GONE for all of them. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec and your client matches on `plan_limit_exceeded:` or a sibling, switch to `code` — the prefix was removed once the only client depending on it had shipped the codes.

THREE PERMISSION codes are described here, and they are the most diffuse of all of them — 106, 51 and 1 call sites respectively, under most mutating and administrative operations in this document:

- `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing. The remedy is a different role, which only an administrator of that farm can grant, and `params.role` is there so a client can name the role the person actually holds rather than guessing.

  Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only. This one comes from a usecase and means the OPERATION needs write. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this.

  Uncoded until #1767, which is why a client reading a cached copy of this spec should treat its absence as "this server predates the code" rather than "this server cannot refuse a write".

- `ADMIN_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not perform this ADMINISTRATIVE action. Params: `role`. 51 call sites, and it refuses four of the six roles — EDITOR, AUDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR.

  **Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which is a different condition and not a variant of this one.** That one comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only: the whole area is closed to this role. This one comes from a usecase and means the route is NOT admin-only — the caller reached the handler legitimately — and this particular OPERATION needs admin. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this check, so a client that shows one sentence for both will tell an EDITOR they lack access to a screen they are looking at.

  Uncoded until #1779. `ADMIN_REQUIRED` was deliberately NOT renamed to make room for it: that code is one of the four reachable on every route and the most likely of all of them to be live in a shipped client, and a clearer name is not worth a breaking change to it.

- `AUDIT_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role may not perform AUDIT actions. Params: `role`. ONE call site, refusing EDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR. Coded in the same change as its sibling rather than on its own merits: three sibling helpers raising two coded refusals and one bare string is the state that invites a reader to assume the bare one is deliberate.

Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. No tenant route can answer either. They are here because that one function is the choke point all of those routes reach and three of their paths are not in this document yet, so a per-operation list would be wrong by omission:

- `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. A key belongs to a farm and authorises nobody in particular, so this is a category error rather than a permission shortfall: retrying with a wider-scoped key cannot work. Use a user session or a bearer token minted for one.
- `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.
- `TENANT_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED` — the request reached the resolver with neither a slug nor an id. In practice this means a session carrying no tenant, so re-authenticating or picking a farm is the way out rather than retrying. The 404 status is historical and kept on purpose: changing it would break a client that already handles 404 here, and the #1712 migration is about the LANGUAGE a farmer reads.

Both carried an English sentence and no code until #1712. The iOS client resolves display from `error.message` and has no `NOT_FOUND` entry, so an uncoded 404 reached a Bulgarian farmer as English — which is the whole reason these are coded rather than merely translated.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. `max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000))`, so it is never 0 — a client that retries immediately on 0 would spend the next window the moment it opens. The same number is in the body as `retryAfterSeconds`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The preset ceiling for this scope, in requests per window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

get.summary: A recorded activity, for a correction to prefill
get.description:
The bare-activity counterpart of `GET /journal/treatments/{treatmentGroupId}/definition` (#2373) — same shape, same ETag, different fields. An activity has no product, dose, pest or quarantine period, and the treatment route refuses a bare handle with `NOT_A_TREATMENT` precisely because prefilling a correction form with an empty product invites a farmer to overwrite a real record with blanks.

The version travels both in the body and as a strong `ETag`.

409.description: - `ACTIVITY_MIXED_AUTHORSHIP` — recorded by more than one person, so it cannot be corrected as a whole. **Binds administrators too**: an activity nobody solely authored has no creator for the edit rule to admit.

put.description:
Owner approved a correction route for резитба, обработка на почвата and прибиране on 2026-10-25 (#2373). Before it, the journal row’s `mayCorrect` already said these were correctable while the only correction route refused the handle.

**Corrects the DAY, the PARCEL SET and, for a harvest, the TOTAL.** Not the kind and not the title, each absent for its own reason, recorded on the request schema rather than left to be discovered. The title in particular would not reach the farmer: a bare activity’s journal title is SERVER-composed from the kind and the parcel, so a corrected `Task.title` would change nothing in «Дневник».

**A parcel in a block the activity never covered is ACCEPTED** (owner, 2026-10-26) and the server mints that block’s task — unlike the treatment correction, whose refusal rests on the БАБХ register printing one table per block. Activities are not in that register, and the whole-farm diary prints ONE row per activity summing its parcels’ areas, so a new block changes nothing about the document.

**The harvest total follows the record, not the row it sits on.** It is stored on one line’s journal entry, and dropping that parcel deletes the entry — which cascades the quantity. So a correction that changes the parcel set rewrites the total onto the surviving canonical entry, exactly once: dropping a parcel never costs a farmer a yield they measured.

Every field optional, and an absent field is not a change — so sending the same body twice leaves ONE correction on the record, because the second send finds nothing changed and writes nothing at all. No version bump either, so an `If-Match` another client holds stays valid.

`If-Match` carries the GROUP version, not a line version: a correction touches every recorded line, so there is no stable tuple of row versions to send back. Present-but-unparseable is a 400; ABSENT is allowed through unguarded, matching every other versioned route here — the loss that admits is a last-write-wins overwrite between two simultaneous editors, recoverable from the correction trail, which stores the whole previous definition.

**Nothing here reaches a regulated document.** Bare activities are excluded from the БАБХ register, so unlike the treatment correction this cannot alter a form a farmer signs. No stock moves either, in either direction.

200.description: The corrected definition, with the bumped version in the body and the ETag.

400.description:
- `HARVEST_TOTAL_NOT_APPLICABLE` — `harvestKg` was sent on an activity that is not a HARVEST. Refused rather than ignored: a quantity silently dropped is a farmer believing they recorded a yield they did not.
- `ACTIVITY_CORRECTION_WOULD_EMPTY` — the set removes every parcel and adds none. That is a withdrawal: it has its own route, its own audit event, and it RELEASES the handle so it stays resumable. Use `DELETE /journal/treatments/{treatmentGroupId}`.

get.description:
Every correction filed against a field activity, newest first, each with when, who, which fields changed and the whole definition as it stood before (#2373).

**The same ENVELOPE as the treatments trail**, field for field — one `readCorrectionTrail` serves both, so they cannot drift — with `previous` holding a `FarmActivityDefinition` instead of a `TreatmentDefinition`. get.description:
Answers whether a treatment was recorded under this handle, and in what state.

**This exists because the write replays a reused key without comparing the body.** A save whose response is lost, followed by an edit, goes out under a NEW key and writes a SECOND treatment if the first had landed. Asking whether the earlier handle exists is the only way a client can tell, so read this before re-sending an edited treatment under a fresh key.

Three answers, and a client needs all three:

| answer | meaning | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` | nothing landed | write afresh |
| `200` `complete: true` | fully recorded | do not write again |
| `200` `complete: false` | PARTLY recorded — see `completedCount` | retry on the SAME handle; the write finishes the rest |

**`complete` counts DONE lines, not lines.** A line is created pending and marked DONE afterwards, and the mark is what writes the ДНЕВНИК entry — so a treatment whose lines all exist but are unmarked is in the register nowhere. Any failure during marking leaves earlier blocks recorded and later ones not, which is the partial state this answer exists for.

Treating it as a 404 writes a duplicate treatment; treating it as an ordinary 200 reports a compliance record the register does not have.

The handle is a PATH segment and not a query parameter on purpose: iOS writes the full URL including the query string to the device log, unsuppressably.

200.description: The treatment, including whether it is complete.

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. Each carries `params` so a client composes its own sentence rather than rendering ours (#1679):

- `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. It resets at the start of the next **UTC** month with nothing to settle, so a client can honestly say "next month" — which is what distinguishes it from the one above, where waiting changes nothing. UTC is stated because it is not local: for a Bulgarian user the reset lands at 02:00 or 03:00 on the 1st (EET/EEST), so copy naming a DAY would be wrong for a few hours each month. Raised by agrent-ios, which got this right before the spec said it.
- `AI_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` — the requested model TIER is above this plan's ceiling. Params: `plan`, `tier`, `ceiling`. Distinct from the budget code on purpose: the refusal is on capability, not on spend, so retrying at `ceiling` succeeds immediately and retrying the same tier never will.
- `MODULE_DISABLED` — a product module is off for this tenant. Params: `module` and `reason`. AVAILABLE is a conjunction (plan-allowed AND tenant-enabled) and `reason` says which half failed, because the remedies differ: `"tenant"` means an administrator of THIS farm can turn it on, `"plan"` means the plan does not include it and no administrator can. Do NOT name an administrator without reading `reason` — telling somebody to ask an admin who cannot help is the defect agrent-ios#241 is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph said exactly that. A client that ignores `reason` should stay neutral; the code alone only means "off".
- `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — this deployment runs self-hosted and exposes no in-app checkout at all. Params: `mode`. Nothing the client or the user can do lifts it; do not offer a retry or a plan picker.

  TWO of the five are TRANSLATED by the server (#1677) — `MODULE_DISABLED` and `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — so their `message` is renderable to a user. The other three still carry an English developer-facing sentence: their Bulgarian needs ICU plural agreement, which the server-side renderer does not yet do, and shipping copy that interpolated a wire identifier (`exchange_listing`, `deep`, `FREE`) into a farmer's screen would have been worse than the English. They are tracked on #1677.

  All five carried a legacy `lower_snake:` prefix at the start of `message` until #1677; that prefix is GONE for all of them. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec and your client matches on `plan_limit_exceeded:` or a sibling, switch to `code` — the prefix was removed once the only client depending on it had shipped the codes.

THREE PERMISSION codes are described here, and they are the most diffuse of all of them — 106, 51 and 1 call sites respectively, under most mutating and administrative operations in this document:

- `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing. The remedy is a different role, which only an administrator of that farm can grant, and `params.role` is there so a client can name the role the person actually holds rather than guessing.

  Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only. This one comes from a usecase and means the OPERATION needs write. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this.

  Uncoded until #1767, which is why a client reading a cached copy of this spec should treat its absence as "this server predates the code" rather than "this server cannot refuse a write".

- `ADMIN_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not perform this ADMINISTRATIVE action. Params: `role`. 51 call sites, and it refuses four of the six roles — EDITOR, AUDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR.

  **Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which is a different condition and not a variant of this one.** That one comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only: the whole area is closed to this role. This one comes from a usecase and means the route is NOT admin-only — the caller reached the handler legitimately — and this particular OPERATION needs admin. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this check, so a client that shows one sentence for both will tell an EDITOR they lack access to a screen they are looking at.

  Uncoded until #1779. `ADMIN_REQUIRED` was deliberately NOT renamed to make room for it: that code is one of the four reachable on every route and the most likely of all of them to be live in a shipped client, and a clearer name is not worth a breaking change to it.

- `AUDIT_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role may not perform AUDIT actions. Params: `role`. ONE call site, refusing EDITOR, READER and MECHANISATOR. Coded in the same change as its sibling rather than on its own merits: three sibling helpers raising two coded refusals and one bare string is the state that invites a reader to assume the bare one is deliberate.

Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. No tenant route can answer either. They are here because that one function is the choke point all of those routes reach and three of their paths are not in this document yet, so a per-operation list would be wrong by omission:

- `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. A key belongs to a farm and authorises nobody in particular, so this is a category error rather than a permission shortfall: retrying with a wider-scoped key cannot work. Use a user session or a bearer token minted for one.
- `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.
- `TENANT_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED` — the request reached the resolver with neither a slug nor an id. In practice this means a session carrying no tenant, so re-authenticating or picking a farm is the way out rather than retrying. The 404 status is historical and kept on purpose: changing it would break a client that already handles 404 here, and the #1712 migration is about the LANGUAGE a farmer reads.

Both carried an English sentence and no code until #1712. The iOS client resolves display from `error.message` and has no `NOT_FOUND` entry, so an uncoded 404 reached a Bulgarian farmer as English — which is the whole reason these are coded rather than merely translated.

delete.description:
Removes a treatment as a whole — its tasks, its ДНЕВНИК entries and the register rows they print (#1777, widened by #2175).

It serves two cases. A treatment that cannot be FINISHED: the write is resumable rather than atomic, so re-sending the same handle completes a partly-recorded one — and if the cause of the failure REPEATS, every retry fails identically and the farmer is left with a treatment that will neither complete nor go away. And a treatment recorded in ERROR, complete or not.

**It ERASES the WHOLE treatment, including register entries already written** for the lines that did complete. The rows are physically deleted — tasks, their journal entries, and the `OperationParcel` register lines that cascade with them. Nothing remains beyond the audit event.

Three rulings in ten days, each reversing part of the last, so the history is worth stating: 2026-10-15 made this route ADMIN-only and INCOMPLETE-only; 2026-10-22 reversed both, defensible then because the delete was SOFT and restorable; 2026-10-24 removed «Кошче» entirely — "what's deleted is deleted" — which removed the very property that justified the wider door. The door stays wide and the safety net is gone, deliberately.

The journal entries are deleted EXPLICITLY, not by cascade. `LogEntry.operationParcel` is an optional relation with no `onDelete`, so Prisma defaults it to SET NULL: without the explicit delete every entry would survive with a null `operationParcelId`, still live and still listed.

| answer | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | withdrawn — the body reports how many tasks, entries and lines it touched |
| `404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` | no treatment under that handle, or it was already withdrawn |
| `403` `TREATMENT_DELETE_NOT_PERMITTED` | not the treatment's creator and not a farm admin |
| `409` `TREATMENT_MIXED_AUTHORSHIP` | recorded by more than one person, so it cannot be corrected or withdrawn as a whole — admins included |

Afterwards the handle stops resolving — this `GET` and `.../farm-record` both answer `404`. There is no deleted-treatment listing and no restore: both routes were removed with «Кошче».

The handle is released for EVERY treatment now, complete or not. It used to be released only for an incomplete one, because a soft-deleted row still occupied `@@unique([tenantId, clientMutationId])` while the replay lookup filtered it out — and keeping it on a complete treatment mattered only so a restore could be exact. A deleted row occupies no key and there is no restore, so both halves of that rule are gone.

Unfinished lines move to `SKIPPED` rather than being deleted, because `OperationParcel` has no soft-delete column and the completion pass already refuses to touch that state.

get.description:
**400 `NOT_A_TREATMENT`** when the handle names a BARE ACTIVITY — pruning, cultivation or harvest (#2316). Such a record has no product, dose or quarantine period, and those are the only fields a correction edits, so there is nothing here to prefill. Gate the correction control on the row’s `kind` rather than discovering it from this response.

Every field of the treatment as it was recorded, plus the GROUP version to send back as `If-Match` on the correction (#2172).

**A sub-resource rather than fields on `GET ../`.** That one is the summary the journal detail view reads — it takes ONE line and selects `completedAt` and `phenophase`. Widening it would put every parcel, every treated area, the product, the dose and both units on the payload of every journal detail read, for the one caller about to open a correction form.

**This is a WRITE-gated read**, in this order: `canWrite`, then SINGLE AUTHORSHIP, then creator-or-admin. So a reader who can see the treatment in the journal gets `403` here. That is deliberate — the body is the whole record and its only purpose is to be edited and sent back.

`409` `TREATMENT_MIXED_AUTHORSHIP` when the handle carries tasks written by more than one person: there is then no single creator for the permission rule to admit, and that binds admins too. The same refusal the withdrawal raises, for the same reason.

`404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown handle AND for a handle whose tasks exist with no lines — the stranded shape a partial write leaves. There is no definition to correct, and saying so beats returning a shell the form would fill with defaults and save as if it were the record.

**Do not probe this to decide whether to OFFER the control.** The journal list already carries a server-computed `mayDelete` over the same population and the edit rule is the same creator-or-admin test; offering a control that 403s is worse than an absent one.

The handle is a PATH segment rather than a query parameter: iOS writes the full URL including the query string to the device log, unsuppressably.

put.description:
**400 `NOT_A_TREATMENT`** when the handle names a bare activity rather than a treatment (#2316): there is no product or dose to correct, and the correction trail records changes to exactly those fields.

Corrects a treatment already in the ДНЕВНИК, atomically across every block it touched (#2172). One transaction writes the tasks, the register lines, the journal entries’ day, a `TreatmentCorrection` trail row and the group version bump — so a correction that fails leaves the treatment exactly as it was.

**What is corrected**: `title`, `applicationTechnique`, `targetNote`, `quarantinePeriodDays`, `phenophase`, `occurredOn`, `productItemId`, `doseValue`, `doseUnitId`, `waterRateValue`, `waterRateUnitId`, and the per-parcel `treatedAreaHa` inside `parcels`.

The last five and the treated area all feed the quantity each journal entry records, so a correction **recomputes that entry** through `computeAppliedQuantity` — the same function `recordInputApplication` used to write it (#2289). Without that, the Дневник would print the quantity of the dose that was replaced, beside the corrected dose, in the same record. A corrected PRODUCT also recomposes the entry’s title — but only where the title is still the one this app composed, so a farmer who retyped their own is not overwritten.

**The parcel list is the SET**, not a patch: a parcel absent from `parcels` is DROPPED and one not already on the treatment is ADDED. A dropped parcel loses its register line AND its journal entry together — `LogEntry.operationParcel` declares no `onDelete`, so Prisma would SET NULL and leave the entry live, listed and printed. An added parcel gets a row and then goes through the same completion path the original lines took, so it carries the journal entry, the audit event and the БАБХ conditions snapshot the register reads for the applicator’s certificates — without which it would print beside its siblings with a blank applicator. A block left with no lines is soft-deleted and its idempotency key released.

**Two shapes are refused.** `400` `TREATMENT_CORRECTION_WOULD_EMPTY` for a list that removes every parcel — that is a withdrawal wearing a correction’s clothes, and the withdrawal has its own route, permission and audit event, and releases the handle so it stays resumable. `400` `TREATMENT_CORRECTION_NEW_BLOCK` for a parcel in a block this treatment never recorded — on principle rather than for want of a mechanism: the ДНЕВНИК prints one table per block, so a block that was never recorded is a treatment that was never recorded, and recording it as its own is the honest shape.

An unchanged list is accepted, so a client may send the whole definition back on every save. #1352 is why — an unconditional refusal of a field the editor always sends broke every farm-profile save from the owner’s phone.

A correction raises the SAME refusals recording would: `REFERENCE_NOT_IN_TENANT` for a product that is not this farm’s (a `400` that does not confirm the row exists elsewhere) or a unit that does not exist, `PRODUCT_IS_SAMPLE_ARCHETYPE` for a sample product, `TREATMENT_AREA_EXCEEDS_PARCEL` for a treated area larger than its parcel, and `TREATMENT_WATER_RATE_INCOMPLETE` for a value without its unit or a unit without its value. A correction must not be a way to put a value into the register that recording it would have refused.

**A correction that changes nothing writes nothing** — no version bump, no trail row, `200` with the definition unchanged. The editor saves the whole form, so a save with no edits is the common case, and it must not invalidate every other client’s `If-Match` or file a row asserting that a farmer altered a regulated record.

**No stock moves.** A diary treatment never deducted any (owner ruling 2026-10-13, carried by `recordedInDiary` suppressing the CONSUMPTION), so a correction has no inventory consequence to reverse. That is what makes this a column update rather than a reversal and a re-application.

Gated exactly as the prefill is: `canWrite`, then SINGLE AUTHORSHIP (`409 TREATMENT_MIXED_AUTHORSHIP`), then creator-or-admin (`403 TREATMENT_EDIT_NOT_PERMITTED`). A blank `title` is `400` `TREATMENT_TITLE_REQUIRED`: the column is NOT NULL, so clearing it would be a database error on a field the form lets you empty.

schema.description:
The `version` you last read from `GET ./definition` — as a bare integer (`5`) or a strong entity-tag (`"5"`), both accepted, which is what the `ETag` on that response already sends back verbatim. Unlike the field-operations lock, the quoted form IS parsed here (#1182).

ABSENT skips the precondition entirely — last-write-wins, matching every other versioned route. PRESENT-but-unreadable is a `400`, never a fall-through: `IF_MATCH_EMPTY`, `IF_MATCH_WEAK_TAG` or `IF_MATCH_MALFORMED`. A caller who sent the header meant to send a version, and guessing on their behalf is how a lost update happens quietly.

The precondition is on the GROUP version, not a line version: a correction writes every line and the set of lines is itself correctable later, so there is no stable tuple of row versions to echo back.

get.description:
Every correction filed against a treatment, newest first, each with when, who, which fields changed and the whole definition as it stood before (#2172).

**This is a READ gate, where `./definition` is a WRITE gate — and that difference is the point.** The prefill requires `canWrite` then creator-or-admin, because its body exists to be edited. The owner asked that a corrected entry show «Коригирано на … от …» with the previous values readable for an INSPECTOR, and an inspector is precisely who the prefill’s 403 is for. Sharing that gate would hide the trail from its audience, so this one is `canRead`: anyone who can see the treatment in the journal can see that it was corrected and what it said before.

No new class of fact reaches a reader. Every `previous` is a definition of the same treatment they are already looking at; the new fact is that a value used to be different, which is what the record exists to state.

**Its own path rather than fields on `./definition`**, for two reasons beyond the gate: the trail is unbounded where a definition is one object, so folding it in would put a growing list on every correction prefill — and a client showing «Коригирано на …» on a journal row needs the trail without wanting an editor.

`404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown handle. Existence is established from the TASKS, not from the trail: a handle with no corrections and a handle that was never used both have an empty trail, and answering `200` with `corrections: []` to the second would confirm a treatment that is not there.

`400` `NOT_A_TREATMENT` for a BARE ACTIVITY handle (#2373). Activities write their trail to the same table, so without this gate the route would answer with `previous` holding a `FarmActivityDefinition` under a contract promising a `TreatmentDefinition` — two shapes on one path with nothing to discriminate on. Read an activity’s history from `/journal/activities/{treatmentGroupId}/corrections`, whose envelope is IDENTICAL: one reader serves both, so they cannot drift.

400.description: - `NOT_A_TREATMENT` — the handle names a bare field activity. Its history is at `/journal/activities/{treatmentGroupId}/corrections`.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

get.summary: The ДНЕВНИК pages for one treatment
get.description:
The Приложение 1 document limited to ONE treatment, across every block it touched: the farm header, a field header strip for each TREATED parcel, and only this treatment’s rows. Produced by the same gatherer and the same renderer as the per-block register, so the layout is identical and the document can be certified.

**Bytes inline.** 200 `application/pdf` with a `Content-Disposition` filename — no job, no URL to poll, nothing persisted. Check for `%PDF` and open it.

A GET where its per-block sibling is a POST, because the handle is this document’s only input and there is nothing to send. The handle is a PATH segment rather than a query parameter: iOS writes the full URL including the query string to the device log, unsuppressably.

The farm header’s block line is EMPTY, deliberately. A treatment spans blocks, so there is no one block to head the document with, and each field strip names its own — which is where the paper form puts it. Printing the first of several would be wrong and would look right.

The observations section prints BLANK: the issue asks for only this entry’s rows, and an observation is a different entry.

`404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` when the handle has no recorded lines — not an empty register, which is indistinguishable from a real document whose treatment recorded nothing, and a farmer cannot tell which they are holding.

Node runtime, 60s budget.
