404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.
- `TENANT_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED` — the request reached the resolver with neither a slug nor an id. In practice this means a session carrying no tenant, so re-authenticating or picking a farm is the way out rather than retrying. The 404 status is historical and kept on purpose: changing it would break a client that already handles 404 here, and the #1712 migration is about the LANGUAGE a farmer reads.

Both carried an English sentence and no code until #1712. The iOS client resolves display from `error.message` and has no `NOT_FOUND` entry, so an uncoded 404 reached a Bulgarian farmer as English — which is the whole reason these are coded rather than merely translated.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. `max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000))`, so it is never 0 — a client that retries immediately on 0 would spend the next window the moment it opens. The same number is in the body as `retryAfterSeconds`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The preset ceiling for this scope, in requests per window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

put.description:
The farm’s own public text — name, tagline, description, oblast and crops. CREATES the draft when there is none, which is what makes the rest of this surface reachable: before this operation existed nothing in the product could write a `FarmBrand`, so `/f/{handle}` served nobody and both sibling routes refused `FARM_BRAND_NOT_FOUND` on every call (#1867).

**A field left out is untouched; an explicit `null` clears it.** That distinction is what an autosaving editor needs — without it, saving a tagline would wipe the description the owner wrote yesterday and never opened today. `crops` has no null form: an empty array IS the cleared state for a list.

**Publication preconditions are NOT enforced here.** A draft may be incomplete, and `displayName` is nullable even though the public page’s column is NOT NULL — refusing a nameless draft would stop an owner saving a tagline before deciding what to call the farm. `PUT .../publication` is where the three refusals bite.

**Editing a PUBLISHED farm refreshes its page in the same call**, reported as `reprojected`. An edit that did not would succeed while changing nothing a visitor sees.

**Per-field visibility (P6.6).** `hideTagline`, `hideAbout`, `hideOblast` and `hideCrops` withhold a field from `/f/{handle}` WITHOUT clearing it. They follow the same omitted-means-untouched rule as the content fields, which is what lets an autosaving editor send one flag without disturbing another — or the text it hides.

There is deliberately no flag for `handle` or `displayName`: both are publication preconditions, so a published farm cannot withhold them. The public projection omits a hidden field entirely, and a visitor cannot distinguish a hidden field from an unset one — which is intentional, because revealing that something is withheld is the thing hiding it is meant to avoid.

**Media.** `logoMediaHash` and `photoMediaHashes` carry CONTENT HASHES returned by `POST /farm-brand/media`, never file ids or URLs. Array order is display order, and removing a hash is how a photograph is withdrawn — there is no visibility flag for images, because the bytes live in storage under an address that does not depend on this field, so clearing it withholds nothing it cannot restore.

**Refusal codes.**
- `FARM_MEDIA_NOT_PUBLISHABLE` — a hash this farm may not publish. ONE code for every reason: not this tenant’s file, not uploaded through `POST /farm-brand/media` (the `farm-media` storage domain), deleted, or never finished storing. They are deliberately indistinguishable, because telling them apart would say whether a hash exists elsewhere in the system. Re-upload the image.
- `FARM_MEDIA_TOO_MANY` — more photographs than a profile may show. The limit is on the wire as `maxPhotos` rather than only in the sentence, so a translated message can name the figure.

Otherwise none of its own — the bounds are schema validation, and the admin check is the usual tenant-role refusal.

get.description:
What the editor renders. Deliberately WIDER than the public page: it carries `published`, `consentedAt`, `consentTextVersion` and `indexable`, which no reader of `/f/{handle}` ever sees but the form has to show.

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

403.description:

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

put.summary: Record consent to publish the farm’s public profile
put.description:
Records that somebody was shown a specific consent text and agreed to it. `PUT .../publication` refuses `FARM_BRAND_CONSENT_REQUIRED` until this has been called, so this is the operation that unblocks publishing.

**Its own operation rather than a field on the content save, deliberately.** Consent is a legal artefact, not editor state. The content route is autosaved, and an autosave that recorded consent would be claiming somebody read something they never saw — the one thing a consent record must not be able to say.

`textVersion` is what makes the record checkable. "They consented" is unfalsifiable once the wording changes; "they consented to v2" can be held against the v2 text. Send the version of the text the sheet actually displayed, not the newest one you know of.

**Re-consenting MOVES the timestamp.** A first-consent-wins rule would leave a farm published against a text nobody alive agreed to.

**Refusal codes.**
- `FARM_BRAND_NOT_FOUND` (404) — there is no draft to consent to. Consent to publish a farm with no public profile is consent to nothing, so save content first.

get.summary: The farm’s A6 share card, as a PDF
get.description:
A 105 × 148 mm (A6) card carrying the farm’s public name, its address as text, and a QR code that resolves to `/f/{handle}`. Intended to be printed and handed out — at a market stall, pinned to a gate.

**A PDF rather than a print stylesheet, and that is a constraint rather than a preference.** `@page` is a document-level CSS rule with no element scope, and the application’s global stylesheet already declares the only one it has (`size: A4 landscape`, inside `@media print`). A second `@page` for A6 would either lose to that rule or re-size every other print surface in the application, depending on nothing more than stylesheet order. Serving bytes also means the Cyrillic face is EMBEDDED, so the farm’s name does not depend on the fonts installed wherever the sheet is printed.

**No image.** Text and the QR only, per the owner’s ruling that the public farm page carries no avatar — a card is the same surface one step further from anyone who could correct it.

`Cache-Control: no-store`. The card embeds the farm’s current public name, and a cached copy would hand out a sheet naming what the farm used to be called.

**Refusal codes.** All three are fail-closed, and stricter than the editor’s on purpose: paper outlives state. A card printed from an incomplete draft points at a dead address for as long as the sheet exists, and there is no equivalent of withdrawing it.
- `FARM_BRAND_NOT_FOUND` (404) — this farm has no public profile yet.
- `FARM_BRAND_HANDLE_REQUIRED` — no public address has been chosen, so there is nothing for the QR to encode.
- `FARM_BRAND_DISPLAY_NAME_REQUIRED` — no public name, so the card would be a QR code and nothing else.
- `FARM_BRAND_NOT_PUBLISHED` — the profile exists but is not public, so `/f/{handle}` does not answer. This is the first operation in the product that requires an ALREADY-published farm; every other write on this model is what gets it there. Call `PUT .../farm-brand/publication` first.

post.summary: Upload an image for the public profile
post.description:
Stores an image and answers its CONTENT HASH. It does NOT publish anything — putting the hash on `logoMediaHash` or `photoMediaHashes` via `PATCH /farm-brand` is what decides whether an image appears, where, and as what.

Two steps on purpose. An upload that also published would make dropping a file onto the page a publication decision, and there would be no way to upload four photographs and then choose two. It also makes a retry safe: the same bytes give the same hash, so a dropped connection does not produce a second gallery entry.

**EXIF, XMP and GPS are stripped** before the bytes are stored (#1812), by re-encoding. On this surface that is the point rather than a precaution: a farmer photographs a field FROM the field, so the GPS tag in that photo is the parcel’s location. Format is preserved and the pixels are unchanged; orientation is baked in first, so a portrait phone photo is stored upright rather than relying on a tag that is about to be removed.

JPEG, PNG and WebP only — narrower than the shared upload allowlist, because only formats the strip pipeline re-encodes may be published. The bytes are AV-scanned before the decode, so a malformed container reaches a scanner before it reaches an image decoder.

The hash is NOT a capability. Holding one does not make an image public: `GET /api/public/media/{hash}` serves it only once a PUBLISHED profile references it, and only this tenant can put it there.

**Refusal codes.**
- `INVALID_FILE` — no `file` part in the form data, or it was not a file.
- `IMAGE_UNREADABLE` — the magic number said image and the decoder disagreed. A different photo, not the same one re-exported.
- `FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` — not a JPEG, PNG or WebP, checked on the bytes rather than the declared type.
- `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `FILE_EMPTY` — the shared upload bounds.

get.description:
ANONYMOUS. No session, no tenant, no credential — a stranger with a shared link browses the same surface.

**Latin and Cyrillic both work, and you do not have to choose.** A farm named «Стопанство Победа» is found by `Победа` and by `Pobeda`. That is not a client-side convenience: the server stores the transliterated form alongside the Cyrillic one, because cross-script trigram similarity is ZERO and no threshold would bridge it. Transliteration follows the Закон за транслитерацията (2009) Streamlined System — the spelling on Bulgarian passports and road signs.

Matching is by SIMILARITY, not equality, and that matters for a real case: «АгроТех» transliterates to `AgroTeh` (`х → h` — transliteration is not translation), so a visitor typing the English-looking `AgroTech` matches nothing exactly and is found anyway.

All parameters are optional. With no `q` this BROWSES: results are ordered by handle and every `score` is 0. With a `q` they are ordered by best match. `oblast` is exact; `crop` is array containment against the farm’s declared crops.

**Bounded at 50 and not pageable.** A visitor who needs more should narrow by `oblast` or `crop`, which is what the filters are for — a public endpoint is not a data export.

Answers a BARE ARRAY. Only published profiles appear, because a row exists in the projection only while a farm is published; withdrawing one removes it rather than flagging it.

**Refusal codes.** None of its own. A malformed `limit` (non-numeric, below 1, above 50) is a `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field; everything else is optional and an absent value is a legitimate request rather than an error.

200.description: Matching farms, best match first. A BARE ARRAY.

get.summary: Fetch an image published on a farm profile
get.description:
ANONYMOUS. No session, no tenant, no credential — a stranger reading a farm’s page fetches its images from here, and a page whose images 401 is not a public page.

**The hash is the content.** `hash` is the sha256 of the stored bytes, so one URL names exactly one byte sequence forever. The response is therefore `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and its `ETag` is the hash itself — a STRONG validator with no bookkeeping, because the name and the content cannot disagree. Changing an image changes the URL, which is the point: a farm that replaces its logo gets a new hash and no cache anywhere has to be told.

**It is in the PATH, deliberately.** iOS logs the full request URL including the query string, unsuppressably, so an identifier in `?hash=` would land in device logs that outlive the request. Do not "simplify" this to a query parameter.

**Publication, not existence, is what it serves.** A hash is unguessable but permanent, so serving any file whose hash matched would be a capability nobody could revoke. This serves a hash only while some published profile references it — withdraw a profile and its images stop resolving in the same step.

Send `If-None-Match` with the hash to get a 304 and no body.

**Refusal codes.** None. Every negative case is ONE 404 with `{ "error": "NOT_FOUND" }` — a malformed hash, a hash no published profile references, a reference whose file is gone, and a file the malware scanner quarantined are deliberately indistinguishable. Distinguishing them would let a caller use the response to confirm which hashes exist, and an unguessable identifier stops being unguessable the moment something confirms a guess. The surface itself 404s when the `social.farm-media` flag is off, for the same anti-enumeration reason.

get.description:
The bytes, with their resolved `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition: inline`. THIS IS THE ANTIVIRUS EGRESS GATE: bytes are written before the scan resolves, so this route is what stops an unscanned or infected file being served, and its 403 is part of the contract rather than an edge case.

TWO distinct 403 codes, because they mean opposite things to the person reading the screen: `FILE_SCAN_PENDING` is "wait and try again" (the scan has not finished, under a strict scan mode), and `FILE_SCAN_REJECTED` is "this file is not coming" (antivirus flagged it). One code for both would leave a client unable to say which happened, so it would have to say neither.

A 404 is `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` for no such document, `DOCUMENT_PURGED` for a tombstone whose bytes are gone (the row is still in the list), or `DOCUMENT_NOT_DOWNLOADABLE` when the upload never reached a stored state — a `FileRecord` left PENDING or FAILED, which is a different thing from a document that has been deleted.

post.summary: Retry a failed Google Drive copy
post.description:
Queues another attempt at copying a document into the farm’s own Google Drive. It does NOT copy: it sets `drive.state` to PENDING and answers immediately, and a sweep running every two minutes performs the copy. So a 200 here means "queued", never "copied" — poll `drive.state` on the row, which becomes COPIED or FAILED.

ADMIN only. The route sits behind `documents.upload` because that is the floor for this prefix, and the usecase requires admin — the copy resolves the farm’s Google credential, and resolving it decrypts and rotates a tenant-wide secret.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.

Each carries a `message`. - `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. The tenant's own ACTIVE exchange listings stay visible to other farms and inbound threads keep arriving — this is the unpaid tenant's own view closing, not a withdrawal.

  The restriction is COMPUTED per request, with no sweep and nothing to settle, so a cleared balance lifts it on the very next request — a client can honestly tell the user to resolve it and refresh. This description deliberately names no remedy beyond that: App Store guideline 3.1.1 keeps the native client from pointing anyone to pay outside the app, so a prescribed destination would be unreachable for one of the two clients (#1490). Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. - `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. - `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing. Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. No tenant route can answer either. They are here because that one function is the choke point all of those routes reach and three of their paths are not in this document yet, so a per-operation list would be wrong by omission:

- `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. Use a user session or a bearer token minted for one.
- `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

Two codes here come from the TENANT RESOLVER rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on every `/api/t/**` route and are the ones worth switching on (#1712):

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. The three are DELIBERATELY indistinguishable and share one code: a response that told them apart would let a caller enumerate farms by slug. So do not offer "check the address" as though the farm were certainly absent — the honest message is that it is not available to this account.
- `TENANT_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED` — the request reached the resolver with neither a slug nor an id. In practice this means a session carrying no tenant, so re-authenticating or picking a farm is the way out rather than retrying. The 404 status is historical and kept on purpose: changing it would break a client that already handles 404 here, and the #1712 migration is about the LANGUAGE a farmer reads.

Both carried an English sentence and no code until #1712. The iOS client resolves display from `error.message` and has no `NOT_FOUND` entry, so an uncoded 404 reached a Bulgarian farmer as English — which is the whole reason these are coded rather than merely translated.

409.description: Nothing to retry, and WHICH of the three it is decides what the caller should do next. `DOCUMENT_DRIVE_ALREADY_COPIED` — a copy exists; show it rather than offering a retry. `DOCUMENT_DRIVE_COPY_IN_PROGRESS` — a copy is on its way; wait. `DOCUMENT_DRIVE_SYNC_OFF` — copying is off for this farm; the remedy is the setting.

426.description: Client too old — the declared `x-agrent-client-version` is below the supported floor. The request was not processed; it is NOT a payload rejection.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. `max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000))`, so it is never 0 — a client that retries immediately on 0 would spend the next window the moment it opens. The same number is in the body as `retryAfterSeconds`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The preset ceiling for this scope, in requests per window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

delete.description: The uploader or an administrator, matching `mayDelete` on the row; anyone else gets 403 `DOCUMENT_DELETE_NOT_ALLOWED`, which a client will normally only see from a STALE list. The bytes go; the ROW SURVIVES as a tombstone carrying `purgeReason: DELETED`, `purgedBy` and `purgedAt`, with the title dropped — the title is KEPT on an expiry, because that is the platform acting on a policy rather than a person asking. Idempotent: a second call on an existing tombstone does not move `purgedAt`, because that timestamp is what an audit dates from. Any Google Drive copy STAYS — it lives in the farm’s own Drive and this product does not reach back into it.
